al-Kalbi said: that is because when God, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to it, it trembles in fear.

The exegetes said: it is shaken as a child is rocked in the cradle, until everything upon it is demolished, and everything on it, including mountains and other things, is broken.

The root of *rajj* in the language is movement; it is said: "I shook him, so he was shaken [his neck was stretched]," and "I shook it violently, so it quivered."

﴿And the mountains are crumbled into powder﴾: that is, they are pounded and ground until they become like flour that is kneaded, and *bassa* among the Arabs is flour or sawiq (roasted grain) that is moistened and taken as provision.

It is related of a thief from Ghatafan that he wanted to bake bread but feared he would be hurried away before baking, so he said: "Do not bake bread, and do not crumble it, and do not delay with the camels, detaining them."

'Ata' said: they are removed by removal. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Saddi said: they are broken by breaking.

al-Kalbi: they are sent off from the face of the earth by sending off. Mujahid: they are ground to powder.

al-Hasan: they are uprooted from their roots and go away, after being solid, hard rock. Its parallel is: ﴿Say: My Lord will scatter them with a scattering﴾ [[Surat Ta Ha: 105.]].

'Atiyya: they are spread out as sand and dust is spread.

Ibn Kaysan: they become a heap of sand, scattered, after having been towering and high.

﴿And they become scattered dust﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the ray of sunlight when it enters through a window.

'Ali (may God be pleased with him): the dust raised by animals.

'Atiyya: what flies off from the sparks of fire. Qatada: the debris of trees.

The common reading is *munbaththan* with a *tha'*, meaning scattered; al-Nakha'i read it with a *ta'*, meaning cut off.

﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: categories. Then he explained who they are, saying, Mighty is He who speaks: ﴿So the companions of the right﴾, who are those who are taken by the right side to the Garden.

al-Dahhak said: they are those who are given their records in their right hands.

al-Hasan and al-Rabi' said: they are those who were blessed and auspicious upon themselves, whose lives were in obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and they are those who follow with excellence.

Then He glorified His Prophet (ﷺ) and said: ﴿What are the companions of the right!﴾ This is like saying: "Zayd, what Zayd is!" meaning Zayd is mighty.

﴿And the companions of the left﴾, that is, the left side. The Arabs call the left hand *sha'ma* (ill-omened).

A poet said:

"The arrow and the bow-string are in your left hands for them,

From this comes "al-Sham" (Syria) and "al-Yaman" (Yemen), because Yemen is to the right of the Ka'ba and Syria is to its left, when [it enters the Hijr] [[Two words are illegible, and the apparent reading is what we have recorded.]] beneath the spout.

They are those who are taken by the left side to the Fire.

It is also said: they are those who were on the left of Adam when the offspring were brought out, and God said to them: these are in the Fire, and I do not care.

It is also said: they are those who are given their records in their left hands.

al-Hasan said: they are the ill-omened upon themselves, whose lives were in disobedience.

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me, Ibn Hamran related to us, my father related to us, Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Dinawari related to us, [.....] [[An illegible word.]] from Ibn ibn al-Jarud, from 'Abd al-Ghafur ibn Abi al-Sabbah, from Ibn 'Ali, from Ka'b, concerning the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near, in Gardens of Bliss﴾. He said: they are the people of the Qur'an, and they are the ones crowned on the Day of Resurrection.

al-Husayn related to me, Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to us, Abu Shu'ayb related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan al-Harrani related to us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Babulti related to us, al-Awza'i related to us, who said: I heard 'Uthman ibn Abi Sawda say: "The foremost (al-sabiqun) are those who are first to go to the mosque and first to go out in the way of God, Mighty and Majestic."

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me, Ibn Majah related to us, Ibn Ayyub related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad related to us, Sayyad ibn Hatim related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Shumayt related to us, who said: I heard my father say: "People are three: a man who began good in the freshness of his youth and persisted in it until he left this world; this is the foremost, the one brought near. A man who began his life with sins and long heedlessness, then turned back with repentance; this is a companion of the right. And a man who began evil in his youth and kept to it until he left this world; this is a companion of the left."

Ibn 'Abbas said: the foremost (al-sabiqun) to the Emigration are the foremost in the Hereafter.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: to the five prayers.

Ibn Kaysan: the foremost are those to whatever God, Glorified and Exalted, calls to.

﴿Those are the ones brought near﴾ to God, ﴿in Gardens of Bliss﴾.

al-Husayn related to me, 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Mawsili related to us, Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-'Attar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Waki' related to us, Shu'ba and Mis'ar related to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, who said: it used to be said [[As in the manuscript; the correct reading is: "yaqulu" (he says).]]: "Go forward, go forward!"

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me, Ibn Majah related to us, Ibn Ayyub related to us, al-Qatwani related to us, Sayyar related to us, Ja'far related to us, 'Awf related to me, a man from the people of Kufa related to me, who said: It has reached me that when a man from the foremost, the ones brought near, goes out from his dwelling in Paradise, there is a light for him by which those beneath him recognize him, and they say: "This is the light of a man from the foremost, the ones brought near."

Makki; it has 1,703 letters, 378 words, and 96 verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Khabbazi related to us from Murra, from the shaykh al-Hafiz Ibn Abi 'Asim, who said: 'Amr ibn 'Uthman related to us, Abu Bakr al-'Attar related to us, al-Saddi ibn Yahya related to us from Shuja', from Abu Tayba al-Jurjani, who said:

'Uthman ibn 'Affan entered upon 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud to visit him during the illness in which he died. He said: "What do you complain of?"

He said: "I complain of my sins." He said: "What do you desire?" He said: "I desire the mercy of my Lord." He said: "Shall we not call a physician?"

He said: "The physician is the one who made me ill." He said: "Shall we not order your provision to be given?" He said: "I have no need of it." He said: "Shall I give it to your daughters?" He said: "They have no need of it. I have instructed them to recite Surat al-Waqi'a, for I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites Surat al-Waqi'a every night will never be afflicted with poverty.'" [184] [[Bughyat al-Bahith: 226; al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/634.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Qasim related to me, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Sha'rani related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Razin related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Attaki related to us, Jarir related to us from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Sayyaf, from Masruq, who said: "Whoever wishes to learn the news of the former and latter peoples, the news of the people of Paradise and the news of the people of Hell, and the news of this world and the news of the Hereafter, let him recite Surat al-Waqi'a."

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

The word *kadhiba* (denial) is recorded by Sibawayh; it is a noun like *'afiya* (well-being), *nazila* (calamity), and *'aqiba* (outcome), according to al-Farra'. Some Arab women used to lull their sons with:

"Stand up, stand up,
for you have found a sleeping slave."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verse 13–29:

﴿ Thullatun﴾ — a host, a multitude, ﴿of the earliest generations﴾, i.e., the past nations; ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾, i.e., the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Upon couches woven [with gold and jewels], interlaced, joined one to another, as the links of a coat of mail are woven, one to another, doubled.﴾ [......] [[Blank space in the manuscript.]] one to another, doubled.

From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"And of the weaving of Dawud, woven tightly, drawn along with the tribe, caravan after caravan."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 13/450.]]

And he also said:

"And a fair one like the mirror, woven tightly, upon her there is a crest above the bosom of the body."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/380.]]

From this is also the "wad'" (girth) of the camel, which is the strap made of thongs when some of it is woven over another, doubled, like the links of a coat of mail.

Al-Kalbi said: The length of each couch is three hundred cubits; when the servant wishes to sit upon it, it lowers itself, and when he sits upon it, it rises.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿mawdunah﴾ means arranged in rows (muṣaffafah), and this is the narration of Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas. It is said: "A brick *mawdun*" when some are arranged upon others.

﴿Reclining upon them, facing one another﴾ in visitation, not looking at the back of one another. ﴿There will circulate among them for service youths (wildan), [who are] eternal (mukhalladun)﴾, i.e., they do not die — from Mujahid. Al-Kalbi said: they do not age, do not grow old, do not diminish, and do not change, and they are not like the servants of this world, who change from one state to another.

Ibn Kaysan: meaning [wildanan mukhalladin] they do not transform from one state to another. Ikrimah: "blessed/pampered."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "adorned with earrings."

The historian said: the earring is also called *khuld*.

The poet said:

"And eternal ones adorned with silver, as if their rears were the wastelands of the dunes."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 3/164.]]

Ali and al-Hasan said: "They are the children of the people of this world; they had no good deeds for which they would be rewarded, nor evil deeds for which they would be punished, because there is no childbearing in Paradise."
[[Kanz al-Ummal: 14/498, no. 39412, where it is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali.]]

And in a hadith: "The children of the disbelievers are servants of the people of Paradise."
[[Ibid., where it reads: "They are the servants of the people of Paradise."]]

﴿With goblets﴾, plural of *kub*, ﴿and pitchers﴾, plural of *ibriq*, named so for the brightness of its color; ﴿and a cup from a flowing spring﴾, wine running; ﴿they will not be affected with headache thereby﴾, i.e., their heads are not aching from drinking it; ﴿nor will they be intoxicated﴾; ﴿and fruit of what they select﴾, i.e., what they choose and desire.

Ibn Finjawayh informed me: Ibn Habash related to us: Dhakkar related to us: Hannad related to us: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a bird having seventy thousand feathers; it comes and lands upon the platter of a man of the people of Paradise, then shakes itself, and from each feather there emerges a color whiter than snow and hail, softer than butter, sweeter than honey, with no color resembling another; then it flies off and departs."
[185] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 14/462–463; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/156.]]

﴿And wide-eyed houris﴾. Abu Ja'far, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and al-Mufaddal read it with a kasra on the waw and the nun, meaning "and with wide-eyed houris," the latter being made to follow the former in case-ending according to the wording, though they differ in meaning, because the houris are not circulated (with drinks). Like the saying of the poet:

"When the beautiful women appear one day, and they have darkened their eyebrows and eyes"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/229.]]

The eye is not darkened (with cosmetic lines), but rather it is painted with kohl.

Another said: "Girded with a sword and a spear," and the like of this is abundant.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Ashhab al-'Uqayli read: (*wa-huran 'inan*) with the accusative, and so it is in the codex of Ubayy, meaning: "and they will be married to wide-eyed houris." Al-Akhfash said: it is in the nominative by the predicate of the attribute, i.e., for them are wide-eyed houris.

It was said: it is a beginning (mubtada'), and its predicate is what follows.

Al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Saqlab related to us: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Bashir ibn Yusuf ibn al-Nadr related to us: Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati related to us: 'Amr ibn Hashim related to us: Sulayman ibn Abi Karimah related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me about the saying of Allah, Azza wa Jall: ﴿wide-eyed houris﴾?" He said: "Houris, white, large-eyed, with big eyes."
[186] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/312; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 3/278, with variation.]]

Ibn Finjawayh informed us: Ibn Saqlab related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khasib related to me: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us: al-Harith ibn Khalifah related to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wide-eyed houris were created from saffron."
[187] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/95; Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/231.]]

Ibn Finjawayh informed me: Ibn Yawdah related to us: Ubayd ibn 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Shurayk al-Bazzaz related to us: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, son of the daughter of Shurahbil, related to us: Khalid ibn Yazid related to us, from Abu Malik, from his father, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant enters Paradise except that he is married to seventy-two wives: two of the wide-eyed houris and seventy from his inheritance from the people of the Fire. There is not a woman among them except that she has a desirable vagina, and he has a penis that does not bend."
[188] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1452, no. 4337.]]

Ibn Finjawayh informed me: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali related to us: 'Uthman ibn Nasr al-Baghdadi related to us: Muhammad ibn Muhajir Abu Hunayf related to us: Halbas ibn Muhammad al-Kilabi related to us: Sufyan al-Thawri related to us, from Mansur or al-Mughirah, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A light shines forth in Paradise, and they say: 'What is this?' They say: 'The light of the smile of a houri who laughed in the face of her husband.'"
[189] [[Tarikh Baghdad: 11/163.]]

It is related that when the houri walks, the sound of the sanctification of anklets is heard from her shins, and the glorification of bracelets from her forearms; the necklace of rubies laughs from her throat, and on her feet are sandals of gold whose straps are of pearls, which chime with glorification.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi used to say: "Propose to a wife whom death does not seize from you, and marry her in a house that the turns of calamities do not ruin, and set up for her a canopy that the fires of misfortunes do not burn."

Mujahid said: they were named *hur* because the gaze is bewildered by them (yahir fihinna al-tarf).

﴿Like hidden pearls, kept in their shell﴾, which is untouched by hands, ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾. ﴿They hear therein no ill speech nor sinful talk, but only the saying: "Peace, peace."﴾ In the accusative of both there are two possibilities: first, an echo (ittiba') of *qil* (saying); second, that it is the object of the verb *qil* (saying), [so that] its accusative is by the falling of the saying upon it: (they hear "peace"). Then he returned to mentioning the abodes of the companions of the right, so he said: ﴿And the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? — among lote trees without thorns﴾, i.e., without thorns in them, as if its thorns were cut off, i.e., severed and removed.

From this is the hadith concerning Medina: "Its thorns are not cut off, nor is its tree pressed."
[[Al-Tibyan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an: 9/496.]] This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Qasamah ibn Zuhayr.

Al-Hasan said: "the hands are not wounded." Qatadah: "it is that which does not repel a hand from it by thorn or distance."

Al-Dahhak, Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is the one laden with fruit.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: its fruit is greater than the *fulal* (a kind of fruit). Ibn Kaysan said: it is that which has no harm in it.

Al-Hasan said: it is not banana, but a tree that has cool, pleasant shade.

Abu 'Ali ibn Abi 'Amr al-Jiri al-Jarshi informed us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Ammar ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, saying: Rashid narrated to us, ḥ [[This letter is a sign placed between two chains to indicate that they share the narrator who follows it; see Mu'jam al-Rumuz wa al-Isharat: 115–116.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Habash narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shha'i narrated to us, saying: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushd ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayra, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding His saying "and raised couches," said: "Indeed their height is like the distance between the sky and the earth, and the distance between the sky and the earth is a five-hundred-year journey." [192] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/240.]]

Abu Umama al-Bahili said: If a couch were thrown from its top to its bottom, it would not settle until after seventy autumns.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "raised" refers to the beds.

It was also said: By "couches" He meant the women, and the Arabs call a woman a "firash" (couch), a "libas" (garment) and an "izar" (wrapper) by way of metaphor, because the couch is the place of women. "Raised" means they are elevated in beauty and excellence above the women of the world.

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying after it: "Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age." Said by al-Hasan, Qatada, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and it is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas; 'Ikrima from him: "mulaqqa" (affectionate). 'Ikrima said: "ghanija" (coquettish, charming).

Ibn Buraydah: al-Sharkala in the dialect of Makka, and al-Maghnuja in the dialect of Madina.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Thabit ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Usama ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding "'uruban": "the good qualities of speech."

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni informed me, saying: Hamid ibn Shu'ayb al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, Mughira narrated to us, from 'Uthman, from Tamim ibn Hizam, who said: It is "the good in marital conduct" (husna al-tab'ul), and the Arabs used to say of a woman who was good in marital conduct, "indeed she is 'uruba," its singular being "'arub."

"Atraban": equal in age.

From Ibn Fanjawayh, Ibn Shanba al-Furati narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise beardless, with white skin, curly-haired, with kohl-darkened eyes, aged thirty-three, in the form of Adam, whose height is sixty cubits by seven cubits." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/343, where it reads "seventy cubits"; and in another wording of his, with variation, p. 295: "sixty cubits."]] [193]

The exegetes said: These are the attributes of the women of this world, and the meaning of His saying "We created them" is: We created them after the first creation, and reports have come to this effect.

Al-Husayn informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Yuqtini narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-'Uqayli narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon 'A'isha, and with her was an old woman from the Banu 'Amir. He said: "Who is this old woman with you, O 'A'isha?" She said: "One of my maternal aunts, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Indeed the old woman will not enter Paradise." That reached the old woman completely. When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned, 'A'isha mentioned to him what the old woman had suffered. He said: "Indeed when she enters Paradise she will be created as another creation." [194] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/419; and al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyya: 199, with variation.]]

Al-Husayn informed me: Abu Zur'a Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Isma'il al-Farisi, resident of Bukhara, narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn 'Amr ibn [Maymun] al-Bukhari narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Musa Ghunjar narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Umm Salama, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age." He said: "O Umm Salama, they are those who died in the abode of this world as old women, white-haired, weak-eyed, with discharge in their eyes; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes them after old age 'atraban (equal in age), upon one birth, in evenness." [195] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 23/368; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/210.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab ibn Shuraik narrated to us: "Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins."

He said: They are the old women of this world; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, creates them a new creation, so that whenever their husbands come to them, they find them virgins. When 'A'isha heard this she said: "Oh, my pain!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no pain there." [196] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/211.]]

Al-Husayn informed me: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi Abu Muslim al-Kajji narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Mubarak narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan: that an elderly old woman [kabira] [[In the manuscript: kabiran.]] came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He admit me to Paradise." He said: "O mother of so-and-so, indeed old women will not enter Paradise." So she turned away, weeping.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Inform her that on that Day she will not be an old woman [[In the source there is an addition: and she will be young on that day.]], for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age.'" [197] [[Tafsir Mujahid: 2/648.]]

And by the chain of al-Musayyab: 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ifriqi narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the women of this world enter Paradise, they will be preferred over the Houris by their prayers in this world.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Tayyib informed us, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Amr ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Harith al-Wasiti in Baghdad narrated to us, saying: Khalad ibn Yahya ibn Safwan al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Aban, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying "Indeed We created them with a special creation": "Your old women in this world, weak-eyed and with discharge, He made them virgins." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/312.]]

And it was said they are the Houris.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-'Uthmani narrated to us, saying: al-'Abbas narrated to us, saying: al-Walid 'Abd Allah ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Houris were created from the glorification of the angels, so there is no harm in them."

[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/519, no. 39468.]] [198] Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age" — 'uruban: ardent lovers of their husbands; atraban: equal in age.

And a shade extended, constant, which the sun does not heat.

Al-Rabi' said: It means the shade of the Throne. 'Amr ibn Maymun said: [it is] a journey of seventy thousand years.

Abu 'Ubayda said: The Arabs say "long time" (dahr tawil) and "long life" ('umr tawil), and of a thing that does not cease: "mamdud" (extended).

Labid said:
"Patience was overcome, and you were not one who turns back — a long-lasting, extended time."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/209. In al-Tabari's Jami' al-Bayan (al-baqa') is given in place of (al-'azaa'): 27/236.]]

Abu Muhammad Mahdi ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan al-'Alawi narrated to us by dictation in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal of the year 389 [AH], saying: Abu Bakr Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us, saying: Zam'a ibn Salih narrated to us, from Salama, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "and a shade extended," he said: It is a tree in Paradise on a trunk; the people of Paradise go out to it, the people of the chambers and others, and they converse at its base, and some of them remember and some of them desire the amusements of the world. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends upon it a wind from Paradise, and that tree moves with every amusement that was in the world.

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Muhammad ibn Habish ibn 'Umar al-Muqri' narrated to us, saying: Dhakkar ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: 'Abda narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it. Recite, if you wish, the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'and a shade extended.'" [190] [[Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 11/417; and Musnad Abi al-Ja'd: 177.]]

"And water poured forth" — flowing, poured out, running constantly, not in a trench, never cut off.

Al-Husayn informed me: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani narrated to us, saying: Khuzayma ibn Ahmad al-Bawardi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, saying: Muzahim ibn Dawud ibn 'Alba [[In the books of biographical criticism: Muhammad ibn Ghalba; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib: 10/90, no. 183.]] said: A brother of mine died, and he was dutiful to his mother. I saw him in a dream, and I said to him: "O my brother, your brother wishes to know what state you have come to?"

He said to me: "I am among lote-trees without thorns, and banana-trees layered with fruit, and a shade extended, and water poured forth."

"And abundant fruit, neither cut off by seasons nor forbidden by price."

Al-Qutaybi said: There is no prohibition upon it as there is upon the orchards of this world. It was also said: the fruit is not cut off when picked; rather, its like grows in its place.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Shayba narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Azraq narrated to us, saying: Rayhan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whatever is cut from the fruits of Paradise, Allah replaces in its place with twice as much." [191]

"And raised couches."

Abu 'Ali ibn Abi 'Amr al-Jiri al-Jarshi informed us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Ammar ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, saying: Rashid narrated to us, ḥ [[This letter is a sign placed between two chains to indicate that they share the narrator who follows it; see Mu'jam al-Rumuz wa al-Isharat: 115–116.]]

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Thabit ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Usama ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding "'uruban": "the good qualities of speech."

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni informed me, saying: Hamid ibn Shu'ayb al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, Mughira narrated to us, from 'Uthman, from Tamim ibn Hizam, who said: It is "the good in marital conduct" (husna al-tab'ul), and the Arabs used to say of a woman who was good in marital conduct, "indeed she is 'uruba," its singular being "'arub."

"Atraban": equal in age.

From Ibn Fanjawayh, Ibn Shanba al-Furati narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise beardless, with white skin, curly-haired, with kohl-darkened eyes, aged thirty-three, in the form of Adam, whose height is sixty cubits by seven cubits." [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/343, where it reads "seventy cubits"; and in another wording of his, with variation, p. 295: "sixty cubits."]] [193]

The exegetes said: These are the attributes of the women of this world, and the meaning of His saying "We created them" is: We created them after the first creation, and reports have come to this effect.

Al-Husayn informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Yuqtini narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-'Uqayli narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon 'A'isha, and with her was an old woman from the Banu 'Amir. He said: "Who is this old woman with you, O 'A'isha?" She said: "One of my maternal aunts, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Indeed the old woman will not enter Paradise." He said: "Indeed when she enters Paradise she will be created as another creation." [194] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/419; and al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyya: 199, with variation.]]

Al-Husayn informed me: Abu Zur'a Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Isma'il al-Farisi, resident of Bukhara, narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn 'Amr ibn [Maymun] al-Bukhari narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Musa Ghunjar narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Umm Salama, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: "Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age." He said: "O Umm Salama, they are those who died in the abode of this world as old women, white-haired, weak-eyed, with discharge in their eyes; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes them after old age 'atraban (equal in age), upon one birth, in evenness." [195] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 23/368; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/210.]]

He said: "O mother of so-and-so, indeed old women will not enter Paradise." So she turned away, weeping.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Inform her that on that Day she will not be an old woman [[In the source there is an addition: and she will be young on that day.]], for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age.'" [197] [[Tafsir Mujahid: 2/648.]]

And by the chain of al-Musayyab: 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ifriqi narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud, who said: When the women of this world enter Paradise, they will be preferred over the Houris by their prayers in this world.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Tayyib informed us, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Amr ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Harith al-Wasiti in Baghdad narrated to us, saying: Khalad ibn Yahya ibn Safwan al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Aban, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying "Indeed We created them with a special creation": "Your old women in this world, weak-eyed and with discharge, He made them virgins." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/312.]]

And it was said they are the Houris.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-'Uthmani narrated to us, saying: al-'Abbas narrated to us, saying: al-Walid 'Abd Allah ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Houris were created from the glorification of the angels, so there is no harm in them."

[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/519, no. 39468.]] [198] Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Indeed We created them with a special creation, and made them virgins, loving, equal in age" — 'uruban: ardent lovers of their husbands; atraban: equal in age.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Husayn informed me: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Isa ibn al-Musawir narrated to us, and the wording is his, and they both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Isa ibn Musa Abu Muhammad and others narrated to us, from Urwa ibn Duwaym, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations﴾, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept and said: "O Prophet of Allah, a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later generations? We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a multitude of the later generations﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar and said: "O son of al-Khattab, Allah has sent down what you said, and He made it: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾."

Umar said: "We are content with our Lord and we affirm our Prophet."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From Adam to us is a multitude, and from me until [the Day of] Resurrection is a multitude, and it will not be completed except by the black men, shepherds of camels, who say: There is no god but Allah." [199] [[Asbab al-nuzul al-ayat (The Occasions of Revelation of the Verses): 270.]]

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: Umar ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning, we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers from their communities. A prophet would come with three from his community, and a prophet with a band from his community, and a prophet with a group from his community, and a prophet with a man from his community, and a prophet with no one from his community at all, until Moses came with a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they impressed me, so I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those of the Children of Israel who surround him.

I said: My Lord, then where is my community? It was said: Look to your right, and there, at the mountain slopes [[al-Zurab: the hills; a zurb is a stone whose base protrudes from a mountain or from hard ground (Kitab al-Ayn: 8/159). It was also said: they are small hills (al-Sihah: 1/174, under z-r-b).]] of Mecca, the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. Then it was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your community who will enter Paradise without reckoning."

He said: Ukasha ibn Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma, rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then another man rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "Ukasha has preceded you with this."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be among them; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. For I have seen people there, pressing upon one another in great numbers."

He said: I said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people who were born in Islam and continued to practise it until they died upon it. This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is not so, but they are those who do not seek cauterization by incantation, do not cauterize, and do not practise omens, and upon their Lord they rely." ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hope that those who follow me from my community will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. [200] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/420, where it reaches to his saying "Ukasha has preceded you with it"; Tarikh Jurjan: 373; al-Mustadrak: 4/578.]]

Abu al-Aliya, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations﴾ means those who preceded this community, and ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾ means from this community at the end of time.

What supports this is:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my community." [201] [[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/249.]]

﴿And those on the left—what of those on the left?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind﴾, a hot wind; ﴿and boiling water﴾, hot water; ﴿and a shade of black smoke﴾, a very black smoke. The Arabs say: "Aswad yahmum" when something is extremely black.

Qutrub recited:
"And what you drank in the valley of [Mecca] ... was sweet water, but like yahmum, my neighbour."

Ibn Buraydah said: al-Yahmum is a mountain in Hell, to whose shade the people of the Fire seek refuge. ﴿Neither cool﴾ but hot, because it is from the smoke of the blazing Hell. ﴿Nor pleasant﴾, nor sweet, according to al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan. A parallel: ﴿of every noble pair﴾. [[Surat al-Shu'ara: 7.]]

Muqatil: "good". Qatada: ﴿not cool﴾ as to its dwelling, ﴿nor pleasant﴾ as to its sight.

Al-Farra said: He makes "karim" follow everything of which he negates an act that carries blame. [[As in their saying: "This is not a spacious house, nor a pleasant one."]]

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Yahmum is one of the names of the Fire. al-Dahhak said: The Fire is black, its people are black, and everything in it is black.

﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent, living in luxury, and they used to persist in the great sin [al-hinth al-azim], that is, in the great wrong, which is shirk.

Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: They used to swear that there would be no resurrection, and that the idols were rivals to Allah, and they persisted in this, and that was their hinth.

﴿And they used to say: "When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be raised? And our forefathers, the earlier ones?" Say: "Indeed, the earlier and the later will all be gathered for the appointed time of a known day."﴾ Then it is said to them: ﴿Indeed, you, O astray, deniers, will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum, and fill your bellies with it, and drink upon it from the boiling water, drinking like the thirsty camels.﴾

The people of Medina, Asim (in the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal), Hamza, al-A'mash and Ayyub recited (shurba) with a ḍamma on the shin, and Abu Hatim chose this reading. The rest recited it with a fatha, and Abu Ubayd chose this.

It is transmitted from al-Kisa'i, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Juraij, that he said: I mentioned to Ja'far ibn Muhammad the recitation of the companions of Abd Allah: (shariba al-hiym) with a fatha on the shin. He said: "Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Budayl ibn Warqa al-Khuza'i to the people of Mina during the days of tashriq and said: 'Indeed, these are days of eating and drinking.'" [202] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/204; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/169.]]

It is said that it is with a fatha on the shin [and ... ] [[an illegible word.]], and both are good dialects.

The Arabs say: "shareba sharban, sharban, sharban" with two ḍammas.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: I heard the Arabs say: "sharibtu sharban," with a kasra on the shin.

As for (al-hiym), it means thirsty camels. Ikrima and Qatada said: it is a disease of camels, in which they are not satisfied [with it] [[In the manuscript: "ma'ha" (with it) rather than "ma'aha" as in the text.]] and never stop drinking until they die. This disease is called al-hiyam. It is said: a thirsty camel-stallion (hamal ahyam), a thirsty she-camel (naqa haymaa), and thirsty camels (ibil hiym).

Labid said:
"I passed over their traces with dishevelled [camels], and with swift, thirsty Mahri camels."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/215.]]

Al-Dahhak, Ibn Uyayna and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Hiym is the level sandy land.

﴿This is their nuzul [welcome/provision], their sustenance and what is prepared for them on the Day of Judgment.﴾ ﴿We created you, so why do you not affirm [the resurrection]?﴾ ﴿Have you considered what you emit [tumnun]?﴾ That is, what you pour into the wombs of the drops of semen.

Abu al-Sammak recited (tamnun) with a fatha on the ta, and both are dialects.

﴿Do you create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ ﴿We have decreed [qaddarna] among you death﴾. Mujahid, Humayd and Ibn Muhaysin recited (qadarna) with a lightened dal; the rest recited it with the shadda. So among you is one who lives until reaching old age, and among you is one who dies young, a child. ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾, unable to destroy you, ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾,

or replacing you with your likenesses, ﴿and in bringing you into being﴾, creating you ﴿in what you do not know﴾, of forms. Mujahid said: "In whatever form We wish."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: ﴿in what you do not know﴾ means: in the crops of birds that are in Barhut, as if they were swallows. Barhut is a valley in Yemen. al-Hasan said: ﴿and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾, meaning: We change your attributes and make you apes and swine, as We did to those before you.

al-Suddi said: We create you in other than your creation.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, the first creation, when you were nothing; ﴿so why do you not remember?﴾ That is, He who is capable of returning you is capable of originating you.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said concerning these meanings: although they are not rejected, what I hold regarding this verse, ﴿and We bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ and ﴿you have certainly known the first creation﴾, is this: I created you for resurrection after death in a manner you do not know, as I wish. That is because you knew the first creation, how it was in the wombs of mothers, and the second is not like that.

﴿Have you considered what you sow?﴾ That is, what you till the earth and work on it, and cast the seed. ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

Al-Husayn informed me: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayyat narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "None of you should say: 'I have sown,' but let him say: 'I have tilled.'" [203] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/218.]]

Abu Hurayra said: Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Have you considered what you till? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

﴿If We wished, We would make it crushed debris [hutaman], dry stalks, of no use for food or sustenance.﴾ He also said once: That is, a plant without wheat in it.

﴿So you would be left [fazaltum] ...﴾ The common recitation is with a fatha on the ẓa'. Abd Allah recited it with a kasra. The original is ẓallaltum, and one of the two lams was deleted for lightness. Whoever recites it with a fatha does so according to the original; whoever recites it with a kasra transfers the vowel of the deleted lam to the ẓa'.

﴿You would be left to fakihun [tafakkahun]﴾. Yaman said: You would regret your expenses, similar to: ﴿so he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾. [[Surat al-Kahf: 42.]]

Qatada: you would be amazed. Ikrima: you would blame one another. al-Hasan: you would regret the disobedience to Allah which made His punishment obligatory for you, so that what befell your crop befell you. Ibn Zayd: you would grieve. Ibn Kaysan: you would be sad.

He said: It is among the addad [words with opposite meanings]. The Arabs say: "tafakkahtu" means "I was made comfortable," and "tafakkahtu" also means "I was made sad."

al-Farra said: tafakkahun and tafakkanun are the same, and the nun is the dialect of Ukl [a tribe among the Arabs; it is also said: 'Adal'].

It is said: tafakkuh means speaking about what does not concern you, and from it comes "fukaha" for jesting.

﴿Indeed we are﴾: Asim, according to the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, recited with two hamzas. The rest recite it as a statement. The meaning of the verse: ﴿you would be left to fakihun﴾, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are burdened with debt [mughramun]﴾. Mujahid and Ikrima said: "We are obsessed with [it]." Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "We are punished, and al-gharam means punishment."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "Exposed to evil." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Destroyed."

al-Dahhak said: We have been burdened in our wealth, and what we spent became a debt upon us. Murra al-Hamadani: "Held to account."

﴿Rather, we are deprived [mahrumun]﴾: limited [mahdudun], [forbidden, mamnu'un] [[In the manuscript: "mumanna'un" with the nun doubled and both vowelled differently.]], cut off from provision; and the mahrum is the opposite of the one given provision.

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: "What prevents you from tilling?" They said: "Drought." He said: "Then do not do it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am the Sower: if I wish, I sow with water; if I wish, I sow with wind; if I wish, I sow with seed.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]] [204] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Have you considered what you till?﴾ and the verses.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds [al-muzn], or are We the senders?﴾ Al-muzn means the clouds; its singular is muzna.

The poet said:
"We are like rain-water: in our reservoir there is no ... and among us there is no one counted as a miser."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]]

﴿If We wished, We would make it ujaj [bitter]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: intensely salty. al-Hasan said: bitter and harsh.

﴿Why do you not give thanks?﴾

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle [tuwrun], striking it out of your flint? Is it you who produced its tree [shajaratuha] from which the fire is struck, which is the markh and the 'afar? Or are We the producers?﴾

﴿We made it﴾, that is, the fire of the world, ﴿a reminder [tadhkira] of the great Fire.﴾

Al-Husayn [...] Ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya, Abd al-Aziz ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part in seventy of the heat of Hell."

They said: "By Allah, it would be enough for us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts, each of which is like its heat." [[Sahih Muslim: 8/149.]] [205]

﴿And a provision [mata'an] for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾: for those who are benefitted, those who dwell in the open land, the qiy [and] the qawa, which is the barren, empty land far from settlement and inhabitants. It is said: "aqwat al-dar" when its inhabitants have left.

The poet said:
"It became desolate and bare, and the winds of the ... changed it, blowing dust hither and thither."
[[The hawj: the wind that blows steadily in its gusts; al-hābī: from the dust-storm (hibā') meaning it rose up; muwār: moving rapidly. The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/264.]]

al-Nabigha said:
"O Dariyya, at al-'Aliya and al-Sanad, it has become desolate there, and the long ages have passed over it."

This is the view of most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: ﴿for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾ means for the people who benefit, all of them, the travellers and those present, who are illuminated by it in darkness, warm themselves by it in cold, and benefit from it in cooking and baking, and by which we remember the Fire of Hell, and so we seek refuge with Allah from it.

al-Hasan said: "for the provision of the travellers, by which they reach their journeys, carrying it in bags and sacks."

al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: it means for the destitute, the needy who have no provision with them: a fire by which they kindle and bake. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: for the hungry.

The Arabs say: "aqwaytu mundhu kadha wa kadha," meaning I have not eaten anything.

Qutrub said: al-muqwi is one of the addad; it may mean poverty and it may mean wealth. It is said: "aqwa al-rajul" when his beasts became strong, and when his wealth became abundant.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.﴾

﴿So no! I swear [la uqsimu]﴾. Most exegetes said: its meaning is "I swear," and "la" is a redundant particle. This is confirmed by the recitation of Isa ibn Umar: (fa-la uqsimu) with clear hamza.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: its meaning is: "So it is not as they say," then he began the oath, saying: ﴿I swear by the setting-places of the stars﴾, meaning the stars of the Qur'an which were sent down ... their scattering and dispersal on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters differed about it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited (bi-mawqi') in the singular; others recited (bi-mawaqi') in the plural, and this is the preferred reading.

﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾, that is, this Book, and this is the place of the oath: ﴿indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ [hasin] [[an illegible word; the closest is what we have reconstructed.]], mighty and honoured.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: it is uncreated. It is also said: it was named "karim" because its ease overcomes its difficulty.

﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: protected, preserved with Allah, Glorified be He, safeguarded from the devils and from everything that defiles.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Husayn informed me: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Isa ibn al-Musawir narrated to us, and the wording is his, and they both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Isa ibn Musa Abu Muhammad and others narrated to us, from Urwa ibn Duwaym, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations﴾, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept and said: "O Prophet of Allah, a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later generations? We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a multitude of the later generations﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar and said: "O son of al-Khattab, Allah has sent down what you said, and He made it: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾."

Umar said: "We are content with our Lord and we affirm our Prophet."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From Adam to us is a multitude, and from me until [the Day of] Resurrection is a multitude, and it will not be completed except by the black men, shepherds of camels, who say: There is no god but Allah." [199] [[Asbab al-nuzul al-ayat (The Occasions of Revelation of the Verses): 270.]]

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: Umar ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning, we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers from their communities. A prophet would come with three from his community, and a prophet with a band from his community, and a prophet with a group from his community, and a prophet with a man from his community, and a prophet with no one from his community at all, until Moses came with a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they impressed me, so I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those of the Children of Israel who surround him.

I said: My Lord, then where is my community? It was said: Look to your right, and there, at the mountain slopes [[al-Zurab: the hills; a zurb is a stone whose base protrudes from a mountain or from hard ground (Kitab al-Ayn: 8/159). It was also said: they are small hills (al-Sihah: 1/174, under z-r-b).]] of Mecca, the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. Then it was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your community who will enter Paradise without reckoning."

He said: Ukasha ibn Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma, rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then another man rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "Ukasha has preceded you with this."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be among them; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. For I have seen people there, pressing upon one another in great numbers."

He said: I said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people who were born in Islam and continued to practise it until they died upon it. This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is not so, but they are those who do not seek cauterization by incantation, do not cauterize, and do not practise omens, and upon their Lord they rely." ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hope that those who follow me from my community will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. [200] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/420, where it reaches to his saying "Ukasha has preceded you with it"; Tarikh Jurjan: 373; al-Mustadrak: 4/578.]]

Abu al-Aliya, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations﴾ means those who preceded this community, and ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾ means from this community at the end of time.

Al-Husayn informed me: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayyat narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "None of you should say: 'I have sown,' but let him say: 'I have tilled.'" [203] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/218.]]

Abu Hurayra said: Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Have you considered what you till? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

﴿If We wished, We would make it crushed debris [hutaman], dry stalks, of no use for food or sustenance.﴾ He also said once: That is, a plant without wheat in it.

﴿So you would be left [fazaltum] ...﴾ The common recitation is with a fatha on the ẓa'. Abd Allah recited it with a kasra. The original is ẓallaltum, and one of the two lams was deleted for lightness. Whoever recites it with a fatha does so according to the original; whoever recites it with a kasra transfers the vowel of the deleted lam to the ẓa'.

﴿You would be left to fakihun [tafakkahun]﴾. Yaman said: You would regret your expenses, similar to: ﴿so he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾. [[Surat al-Kahf: 42.]]

Qatada: you would be amazed. Ikrima: you would blame one another. al-Hasan: you would regret the disobedience to Allah which made His punishment obligatory for you, so that what befell your crop befell you. Ibn Zayd: you would grieve. Ibn Kaysan: you would be sad.

He said: It is among the addad [words with opposite meanings]. The Arabs say: "tafakkahtu" means "I was made comfortable," and "tafakkahtu" also means "I was made sad."

al-Farra said: tafakkahun and tafakkanun are the same, and the nun is the dialect of Ukl [a tribe among the Arabs; it is also said: 'Adal'].

It is said: tafakkuh means speaking about what does not concern you, and from it comes "fukaha" for jesting.

﴿Indeed we are﴾: Asim, according to the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, recited with two hamzas. The rest recite it as a statement. The meaning of the verse: ﴿you would be left to fakihun﴾, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are burdened with debt [mughramun]﴾. Mujahid and Ikrima said: "We are obsessed with [it]." Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "We are punished, and al-gharam means punishment."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "Exposed to evil." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Destroyed."

al-Dahhak said: We have been burdened in our wealth, and what we spent became a debt upon us. Murra al-Hamadani: "Held to account."

﴿Rather, we are deprived [mahrumun]﴾: limited [mahdudun], [forbidden, mamnu'un] [[In the manuscript: "mumanna'un" with the nun doubled and both vowelled differently.]], cut off from provision; and the mahrum is the opposite of the one given provision.

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: "What prevents you from tilling?" They said: "Drought." He said: "Then do not do it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am the Sower: if I wish, I sow with water; if I wish, I sow with wind; if I wish, I sow with seed.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]] [204] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Have you considered what you till?﴾ and the verses.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds [al-muzn], or are We the senders?﴾ Al-muzn means the clouds; its singular is muzna.

The poet said:
"We are like rain-water: in our reservoir there is no ... and among us there is no one counted as a miser."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]]

﴿If We wished, We would make it ujaj [bitter]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: intensely salty. al-Hasan said: bitter and harsh.

﴿Why do you not give thanks?﴾

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle [tuwrun], striking it out of your flint? Is it you who produced its tree [shajaratuha] from which the fire is struck, which is the markh and the 'afar? Or are We the producers?﴾

﴿We made it﴾, that is, the fire of the world, ﴿a reminder [tadhkira] of the great Fire.﴾

Al-Husayn [...] Ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya, Abd al-Aziz ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part in seventy of the heat of Hell."

They said: "By Allah, it would be enough for us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts, each of which is like its heat." [[Sahih Muslim: 8/149.]] [205]

﴿And a provision [mata'an] for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾: for those who are benefitted, those who dwell in the open land, the qiy [and] the qawa, which is the barren, empty land far from settlement and inhabitants. It is said: "aqwat al-dar" when its inhabitants have left.

The poet said:
"It became desolate and bare, and the winds of the ... changed it, blowing dust hither and thither."
[[The hawj: the wind that blows steadily in its gusts; al-hābī: from the dust-storm (hibā') meaning it rose up; muwār: moving rapidly. The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/264.]]

al-Nabigha said:
"O Dariyya, at al-'Aliya and al-Sanad, it has become desolate there, and the long ages have passed over it."

This is the view of most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: ﴿for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾ means for the people who benefit, all of them, the travellers and those present, who are illuminated by it in darkness, warm themselves by it in cold, and benefit from it in cooking and baking, and by which we remember the Fire of Hell, and so we seek refuge with Allah from it.

al-Hasan said: "for the provision of the travellers, by which they reach their journeys, carrying it in bags and sacks."

al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: it means for the destitute, the needy who have no provision with them: a fire by which they kindle and bake. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: for the hungry.

The Arabs say: "aqwaytu mundhu kadha wa kadha," meaning I have not eaten anything.

Qutrub said: al-muqwi is one of the addad; it may mean poverty and it may mean wealth. It is said: "aqwa al-rajul" when his beasts became strong, and when his wealth became abundant.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.﴾

﴿So no! I swear [la uqsimu]﴾. Most exegetes said: its meaning is "I swear," and "la" is a redundant particle. This is confirmed by the recitation of Isa ibn Umar: (fa-la uqsimu) with clear hamza.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: its meaning is: "So it is not as they say," then he began the oath, saying: ﴿I swear by the setting-places of the stars﴾, meaning the stars of the Qur'an which were sent down ... their scattering and dispersal on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters differed about it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited (bi-mawqi') in the singular; others recited (bi-mawaqi') in the plural, and this is the preferred reading.

﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾, that is, this Book, and this is the place of the oath: ﴿indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ [hasin] [[an illegible word; the closest is what we have reconstructed.]], mighty and honoured.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: it is uncreated. It is also said: it was named "karim" because its ease overcomes its difficulty.

﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: protected, preserved with Allah, Glorified be He, safeguarded from the devils and from everything that defiles.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Husayn informed me: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Isa ibn al-Musawir narrated to us, and the wording is his, and they both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Isa ibn Musa Abu Muhammad and others narrated to us, from Urwa ibn Duwaym, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations﴾, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept and said: "O Prophet of Allah, a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later generations? We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a multitude of the later generations﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar and said: "O son of al-Khattab, Allah has sent down what you said, and He made it: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾."

Umar said: "We are content with our Lord and we affirm our Prophet."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From Adam to us is a multitude, and from me until [the Day of] Resurrection is a multitude, and it will not be completed except by the black men, shepherds of camels, who say: There is no god but Allah." [199] [[Asbab al-nuzul al-ayat (The Occasions of Revelation of the Verses): 270.]]

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: Umar ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning, we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers from their communities. A prophet would come with three from his community, and a prophet with a band from his community, and a prophet with a group from his community, and a prophet with a man from his community, and a prophet with no one from his community at all, until Moses came with a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they impressed me, so I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those of the Children of Israel who surround him.

I said: My Lord, then where is my community? It was said: Look to your right, and there, at the mountain slopes [[al-Zurab: the hills; a zurb is a stone whose base protrudes from a mountain or from hard ground (Kitab al-Ayn: 8/159). It was also said: they are small hills (al-Sihah: 1/174, under z-r-b).]] of Mecca, the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. Then it was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your community who will enter Paradise without reckoning."

He said: Ukasha ibn Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma, rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then another man rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "Ukasha has preceded you with this."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be among them; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. For I have seen people there, pressing upon one another in great numbers."

He said: I said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people who were born in Islam and continued to practise it until they died upon it. This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is not so, but they are those who do not seek cauterization by incantation, do not cauterize, and do not practise omens, and upon their Lord they rely." ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hope that those who follow me from my community will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. [200] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/420, where it reaches to his saying "Ukasha has preceded you with it"; Tarikh Jurjan: 373; al-Mustadrak: 4/578.]]

Abu al-Aliya, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations﴾ means those who preceded this community, and ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾ means from this community at the end of time.

What supports this is:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my community." [201] [[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/249.]]

﴿And those on the left—what of those on the left?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind﴾, a hot wind; ﴿and boiling water﴾, hot water; ﴿and a shade of black smoke﴾, a very black smoke. The Arabs say: "Aswad yahmum" when something is extremely black.

Qutrub recited:
"And what you drank in the valley of [Mecca] ... was sweet water, but like yahmum, my neighbour."

Ibn Buraydah said: al-Yahmum is a mountain in Hell, to whose shade the people of the Fire seek refuge. ﴿Neither cool﴾ but hot, because it is from the smoke of the blazing Hell. ﴿Nor pleasant﴾, nor sweet, according to al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan. A parallel: ﴿of every noble pair﴾. [[Surat al-Shu'ara: 7.]]

Muqatil: "good". Qatada: ﴿not cool﴾ as to its dwelling, ﴿nor pleasant﴾ as to its sight.

Al-Farra said: He makes "karim" follow everything of which he negates an act that carries blame. [[As in their saying: "This is not a spacious house, nor a pleasant one."]]

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Yahmum is one of the names of the Fire. al-Dahhak said: The Fire is black, its people are black, and everything in it is black.

﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent, living in luxury, and they used to persist in the great sin [al-hinth al-azim], that is, in the great wrong, which is shirk.

Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: They used to swear that there would be no resurrection, and that the idols were rivals to Allah, and they persisted in this, and that was their hinth.

﴿And they used to say: "When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be raised? And our forefathers, the earlier ones?" Say: "Indeed, the earlier and the later will all be gathered for the appointed time of a known day."﴾ Then it is said to them: ﴿Indeed, you, O astray, deniers, will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum, and fill your bellies with it, and drink upon it from the boiling water, drinking like the thirsty camels.﴾

The people of Medina, Asim (in the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal), Hamza, al-A'mash and Ayyub recited (shurba) with a ḍamma on the shin, and Abu Hatim chose this reading. The rest recited it with a fatha, and Abu Ubayd chose this.

It is transmitted from al-Kisa'i, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Juraij, that he said: I mentioned to Ja'far ibn Muhammad the recitation of the companions of Abd Allah: (shariba al-hiym) with a fatha on the shin. He said: "Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Budayl ibn Warqa al-Khuza'i to the people of Mina during the days of tashriq and said: 'Indeed, these are days of eating and drinking.'" [202] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/204; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/169.]]

It is said that it is with a fatha on the shin [and ... ] [[an illegible word.]], and both are good dialects.

The Arabs say: "shareba sharban, sharban, sharban" with two ḍammas.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: I heard the Arabs say: "sharibtu sharban," with a kasra on the shin.

As for (al-hiym), it means thirsty camels. Ikrima and Qatada said: it is a disease of camels, in which they are not satisfied [with it] [[In the manuscript: "ma'ha" (with it) rather than "ma'aha" as in the text.]] and never stop drinking until they die. This disease is called al-hiyam. It is said: a thirsty camel-stallion (hamal ahyam), a thirsty she-camel (naqa haymaa), and thirsty camels (ibil hiym).

Labid said:
"I passed over their traces with dishevelled [camels], and with swift, thirsty Mahri camels."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/215.]]

Al-Dahhak, Ibn Uyayna and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Hiym is the level sandy land.

﴿This is their nuzul [welcome/provision], their sustenance and what is prepared for them on the Day of Judgment.﴾ ﴿We created you, so why do you not affirm [the resurrection]?﴾ ﴿Have you considered what you emit [tumnun]?﴾ That is, what you pour into the wombs of the drops of semen.

Abu al-Sammak recited (tamnun) with a fatha on the ta, and both are dialects.

﴿Do you create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ ﴿We have decreed [qaddarna] among you death﴾. Mujahid, Humayd and Ibn Muhaysin recited (qadarna) with a lightened dal; the rest recited it with the shadda. So among you is one who lives until reaching old age, and among you is one who dies young, a child. ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾, unable to destroy you, ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾,

or replacing you with your likenesses, ﴿and in bringing you into being﴾, creating you ﴿in what you do not know﴾, of forms. Mujahid said: "In whatever form We wish."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: ﴿in what you do not know﴾ means: in the crops of birds that are in Barhut, as if they were swallows. Barhut is a valley in Yemen. al-Hasan said: ﴿and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾, meaning: We change your attributes and make you apes and swine, as We did to those before you.

al-Suddi said: We create you in other than your creation.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, the first creation, when you were nothing; ﴿so why do you not remember?﴾ That is, He who is capable of returning you is capable of originating you.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said concerning these meanings: although they are not rejected, what I hold regarding this verse, ﴿and We bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ and ﴿you have certainly known the first creation﴾, is this: I created you for resurrection after death in a manner you do not know, as I wish. That is because you knew the first creation, how it was in the wombs of mothers, and the second is not like that.

﴿Have you considered what you sow?﴾ That is, what you till the earth and work on it, and cast the seed. ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

Al-Husayn informed me: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayyat narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "None of you should say: 'I have sown,' but let him say: 'I have tilled.'"
