﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: protected, preserved with Allah, Glorified be He, safeguarded from the devils and from everything that defiles.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Husayn informed me: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Isa ibn al-Musawir narrated to us, and the wording is his, and they both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Isa ibn Musa Abu Muhammad and others narrated to us, from Urwa ibn Duwaym, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations﴾, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept and said: "O Prophet of Allah, a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later generations? We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a multitude of the later generations﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar and said: "O son of al-Khattab, Allah has sent down what you said, and He made it: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾."

Umar said: "We are content with our Lord and we affirm our Prophet."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From Adam to us is a multitude, and from me until [the Day of] Resurrection is a multitude, and it will not be completed except by the black men, shepherds of camels, who say: There is no god but Allah." [199] [[Asbab al-nuzul al-ayat (The Occasions of Revelation of the Verses): 270.]]

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: Umar ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning, we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers from their communities. A prophet would come with three from his community, and a prophet with a band from his community, and a prophet with a group from his community, and a prophet with a man from his community, and a prophet with no one from his community at all, until Moses came with a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they impressed me, so I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those of the Children of Israel who surround him.

I said: My Lord, then where is my community? It was said: Look to your right, and there, at the mountain slopes [[al-Zurab: the hills; a zurb is a stone whose base protrudes from a mountain or from hard ground (Kitab al-Ayn: 8/159). It was also said: they are small hills (al-Sihah: 1/174, under z-r-b).]] of Mecca, the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. Then it was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your community who will enter Paradise without reckoning."

He said: Ukasha ibn Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma, rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then another man rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "Ukasha has preceded you with this."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be among them; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. For I have seen people there, pressing upon one another in great numbers."

He said: I said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people who were born in Islam and continued to practise it until they died upon it. This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is not so, but they are those who do not seek cauterization by incantation, do not cauterize, and do not practise omens, and upon their Lord they rely." ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hope that those who follow me from my community will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. [200] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/420, where it reaches to his saying "Ukasha has preceded you with it"; Tarikh Jurjan: 373; al-Mustadrak: 4/578.]]

Abu al-Aliya, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations﴾ means those who preceded this community, and ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾ means from this community at the end of time.

What supports this is:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my community." [201] [[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/249.]]

﴿And those on the left—what of those on the left?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind﴾, a hot wind; ﴿and boiling water﴾, hot water; ﴿and a shade of black smoke﴾, a very black smoke. The Arabs say: "Aswad yahmum" when something is extremely black.

Qutrub recited:
"And what you drank in the valley of [Mecca] ... was sweet water, but like yahmum, my neighbour."

Ibn Buraydah said: al-Yahmum is a mountain in Hell, to whose shade the people of the Fire seek refuge. ﴿Neither cool﴾ but hot, because it is from the smoke of the blazing Hell. ﴿Nor pleasant﴾, nor sweet, according to al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan. A parallel: ﴿of every noble pair﴾. [[Surat al-Shu'ara: 7.]]

Muqatil: "good". Qatada: ﴿not cool﴾ as to its dwelling, ﴿nor pleasant﴾ as to its sight.

Al-Farra said: He makes "karim" follow everything of which he negates an act that carries blame. [[As in their saying: "This is not a spacious house, nor a pleasant one."]]

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Yahmum is one of the names of the Fire. al-Dahhak said: The Fire is black, its people are black, and everything in it is black.

﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent, living in luxury, and they used to persist in the great sin [al-hinth al-azim], that is, in the great wrong, which is shirk.

Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: They used to swear that there would be no resurrection, and that the idols were rivals to Allah, and they persisted in this, and that was their hinth.

﴿And they used to say: "When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be raised? And our forefathers, the earlier ones?" Say: "Indeed, the earlier and the later will all be gathered for the appointed time of a known day."﴾ Then it is said to them: ﴿Indeed, you, O astray, deniers, will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum, and fill your bellies with it, and drink upon it from the boiling water, drinking like the thirsty camels.﴾

The people of Medina, Asim (in the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal), Hamza, al-A'mash and Ayyub recited (shurba) with a ḍamma on the shin, and Abu Hatim chose this reading. The rest recited it with a fatha, and Abu Ubayd chose this.

It is transmitted from al-Kisa'i, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Juraij, that he said: I mentioned to Ja'far ibn Muhammad the recitation of the companions of Abd Allah: (shariba al-hiym) with a fatha on the shin. He said: "Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Budayl ibn Warqa al-Khuza'i to the people of Mina during the days of tashriq and said: 'Indeed, these are days of eating and drinking.'" [202] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/204; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/169.]]

It is said that it is with a fatha on the shin [and ... ] [[an illegible word.]], and both are good dialects.

The Arabs say: "shareba sharban, sharban, sharban" with two ḍammas.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: I heard the Arabs say: "sharibtu sharban," with a kasra on the shin.

As for (al-hiym), it means thirsty camels. Ikrima and Qatada said: it is a disease of camels, in which they are not satisfied [with it] [[In the manuscript: "ma'ha" (with it) rather than "ma'aha" as in the text.]] and never stop drinking until they die. This disease is called al-hiyam. It is said: a thirsty camel-stallion (hamal ahyam), a thirsty she-camel (naqa haymaa), and thirsty camels (ibil hiym).

Labid said:
"I passed over their traces with dishevelled [camels], and with swift, thirsty Mahri camels."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/215.]]

Al-Dahhak, Ibn Uyayna and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Hiym is the level sandy land.

﴿This is their nuzul [welcome/provision], their sustenance and what is prepared for them on the Day of Judgment.﴾ ﴿We created you, so why do you not affirm [the resurrection]?﴾ ﴿Have you considered what you emit [tumnun]?﴾ That is, what you pour into the wombs of the drops of semen.

Abu al-Sammak recited (tamnun) with a fatha on the ta, and both are dialects.

﴿Do you create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ ﴿We have decreed [qaddarna] among you death﴾. Mujahid, Humayd and Ibn Muhaysin recited (qadarna) with a lightened dal; the rest recited it with the shadda. So among you is one who lives until reaching old age, and among you is one who dies young, a child. ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾, unable to destroy you, ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾,

or replacing you with your likenesses, ﴿and in bringing you into being﴾, creating you ﴿in what you do not know﴾, of forms. Mujahid said: "In whatever form We wish."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: ﴿in what you do not know﴾ means: in the crops of birds that are in Barhut, as if they were swallows. Barhut is a valley in Yemen. al-Hasan said: ﴿and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾, meaning: We change your attributes and make you apes and swine, as We did to those before you.

al-Suddi said: We create you in other than your creation.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, the first creation, when you were nothing; ﴿so why do you not remember?﴾ That is, He who is capable of returning you is capable of originating you.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said concerning these meanings: although they are not rejected, what I hold regarding this verse, ﴿and We bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ and ﴿you have certainly known the first creation﴾, is this: I created you for resurrection after death in a manner you do not know, as I wish. That is because you knew the first creation, how it was in the wombs of mothers, and the second is not like that.

﴿Have you considered what you sow?﴾ That is, what you till the earth and work on it, and cast the seed. ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

Al-Husayn informed me: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayyat narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "None of you should say: 'I have sown,' but let him say: 'I have tilled.'" [203] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/218.]]

Abu Hurayra said: Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Have you considered what you till? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

﴿If We wished, We would make it crushed debris [hutaman], dry stalks, of no use for food or sustenance.﴾ He also said once: That is, a plant without wheat in it.

﴿So you would be left [fazaltum] ...﴾ The common recitation is with a fatha on the ẓa'. Abd Allah recited it with a kasra. The original is ẓallaltum, and one of the two lams was deleted for lightness. Whoever recites it with a fatha does so according to the original; whoever recites it with a kasra transfers the vowel of the deleted lam to the ẓa'.

﴿You would be left to fakihun [tafakkahun]﴾. Yaman said: You would regret your expenses, similar to: ﴿so he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾. [[Surat al-Kahf: 42.]]

Qatada: you would be amazed. Ikrima: you would blame one another. al-Hasan: you would regret the disobedience to Allah which made His punishment obligatory for you, so that what befell your crop befell you. Ibn Zayd: you would grieve. Ibn Kaysan: you would be sad.

He said: It is among the addad [words with opposite meanings]. The Arabs say: "tafakkahtu" means "I was made comfortable," and "tafakkahtu" also means "I was made sad."

al-Farra said: tafakkahun and tafakkanun are the same, and the nun is the dialect of Ukl [a tribe among the Arabs; it is also said: 'Adal'].

It is said: tafakkuh means speaking about what does not concern you, and from it comes "fukaha" for jesting.

﴿Indeed we are﴾: Asim, according to the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, recited with two hamzas. The rest recite it as a statement. The meaning of the verse: ﴿you would be left to fakihun﴾, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are burdened with debt [mughramun]﴾. Mujahid and Ikrima said: "We are obsessed with [it]." Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "We are punished, and al-gharam means punishment."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "Exposed to evil." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Destroyed."

al-Dahhak said: We have been burdened in our wealth, and what we spent became a debt upon us. Murra al-Hamadani: "Held to account."

﴿Rather, we are deprived [mahrumun]﴾: limited [mahdudun], [forbidden, mamnu'un] [[In the manuscript: "mumanna'un" with the nun doubled and both vowelled differently.]], cut off from provision; and the mahrum is the opposite of the one given provision.

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: "What prevents you from tilling?" They said: "Drought." He said: "Then do not do it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am the Sower: if I wish, I sow with water; if I wish, I sow with wind; if I wish, I sow with seed.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]] [204] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Have you considered what you till?﴾ and the verses.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds [al-muzn], or are We the senders?﴾ Al-muzn means the clouds; its singular is muzna.

The poet said:
"We are like rain-water: in our reservoir there is no ... and among us there is no one counted as a miser."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]]

﴿If We wished, We would make it ujaj [bitter]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: intensely salty. al-Hasan said: bitter and harsh.

﴿Why do you not give thanks?﴾

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle [tuwrun], striking it out of your flint? Is it you who produced its tree [shajaratuha] from which the fire is struck, which is the markh and the 'afar? Or are We the producers?﴾

﴿We made it﴾, that is, the fire of the world, ﴿a reminder [tadhkira] of the great Fire.﴾

Al-Husayn [...] Ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya, Abd al-Aziz ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part in seventy of the heat of Hell."

They said: "By Allah, it would be enough for us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts, each of which is like its heat." [[Sahih Muslim: 8/149.]] [205]

﴿And a provision [mata'an] for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾: for those who are benefitted, those who dwell in the open land, the qiy [and] the qawa, which is the barren, empty land far from settlement and inhabitants. It is said: "aqwat al-dar" when its inhabitants have left.

The poet said:
"It became desolate and bare, and the winds of the ... changed it, blowing dust hither and thither."
[[The hawj: the wind that blows steadily in its gusts; al-hābī: from the dust-storm (hibā') meaning it rose up; muwār: moving rapidly. The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/264.]]

al-Nabigha said:
"O Dariyya, at al-'Aliya and al-Sanad, it has become desolate there, and the long ages have passed over it."

This is the view of most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: ﴿for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾ means for the people who benefit, all of them, the travellers and those present, who are illuminated by it in darkness, warm themselves by it in cold, and benefit from it in cooking and baking, and by which we remember the Fire of Hell, and so we seek refuge with Allah from it.

al-Hasan said: "for the provision of the travellers, by which they reach their journeys, carrying it in bags and sacks."

al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: it means for the destitute, the needy who have no provision with them: a fire by which they kindle and bake. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: for the hungry.

The Arabs say: "aqwaytu mundhu kadha wa kadha," meaning I have not eaten anything.

Qutrub said: al-muqwi is one of the addad; it may mean poverty and it may mean wealth. It is said: "aqwa al-rajul" when his beasts became strong, and when his wealth became abundant.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.﴾

﴿So no! I swear [la uqsimu]﴾. Most exegetes said: its meaning is "I swear," and "la" is a redundant particle. This is confirmed by the recitation of Isa ibn Umar: (fa-la uqsimu) with clear hamza.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: its meaning is: "So it is not as they say," then he began the oath, saying: ﴿I swear by the setting-places of the stars﴾, meaning the stars of the Qur'an which were sent down ... their scattering and dispersal on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters differed about it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited (bi-mawqi') in the singular; others recited (bi-mawaqi') in the plural, and this is the preferred reading.

﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾, that is, this Book, and this is the place of the oath: ﴿indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ [hasin] [[an illegible word; the closest is what we have reconstructed.]], mighty and honoured.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: it is uncreated. It is also said: it was named "karim" because its ease overcomes its difficulty.

﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: protected, preserved with Allah, Glorified be He, safeguarded from the devils and from everything that defiles.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Ibn Kaysan said: al-Yahmum is one of the names of the Fire. al-Dahhak said: The Fire is black, its people are black, and everything in it is black.

﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent, living in luxury, and they used to persist in the great sin [al-hinth al-azim], that is, in the great wrong, which is shirk.

Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: They used to swear that there would be no resurrection, and that the idols were rivals to Allah, and they persisted in this, and that was their hinth.

﴿And they used to say: "When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be raised? And our forefathers, the earlier ones?" Say: "Indeed, the earlier and the later will all be gathered for the appointed time of a known day."﴾ Then it is said to them: ﴿Indeed, you, O astray, deniers, will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum, and fill your bellies with it, and drink upon it from the boiling water, drinking like the thirsty camels.﴾

The people of Medina, Asim (in the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal), Hamza, al-A'mash and Ayyub recited (shurba) with a ḍamma on the shin, and Abu Hatim chose this reading. The rest recited it with a fatha, and Abu Ubayd chose this.

It is transmitted from al-Kisa'i, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Juraij, that he said: I mentioned to Ja'far ibn Muhammad the recitation of the companions of Abd Allah: (shariba al-hiym) with a fatha on the shin. He said: "Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Budayl ibn Warqa al-Khuza'i to the people of Mina during the days of tashriq and said: 'Indeed, these are days of eating and drinking.'" [202] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/204; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/169.]]

It is said that it is with a fatha on the shin [and ... ] [[an illegible word.]], and both are good dialects.

The Arabs say: "shareba sharban, sharban, sharban" with two ḍammas.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: I heard the Arabs say: "sharibtu sharban," with a kasra on the shin.

As for (al-hiym), it means thirsty camels. Ikrima and Qatada said: it is a disease of camels, in which they are not satisfied [with it] [[In the manuscript: "ma'ha" (with it) rather than "ma'aha" as in the text.]] and never stop drinking until they die. This disease is called al-hiyam. It is said: a thirsty camel-stallion (hamal ahyam), a thirsty she-camel (naqa haymaa), and thirsty camels (ibil hiym).

Labid said:
"I passed over their traces with dishevelled [camels], and with swift, thirsty Mahri camels."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/215.]]

Al-Dahhak, Ibn Uyayna and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Hiym is the level sandy land.

﴿This is their nuzul [welcome/provision], their sustenance and what is prepared for them on the Day of Judgment.﴾ ﴿We created you, so why do you not affirm [the resurrection]?﴾ ﴿Have you considered what you emit [tumnun]?﴾ That is, what you pour into the wombs of the drops of semen.

Abu al-Sammak recited (tamnun) with a fatha on the ta, and both are dialects.

﴿Do you create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ ﴿We have decreed [qaddarna] among you death﴾. Mujahid, Humayd and Ibn Muhaysin recited (qadarna) with a lightened dal; the rest recited it with the shadda. So among you is one who lives until reaching old age, and among you is one who dies young, a child. ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾, unable to destroy you, ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾,

or replacing you with your likenesses, ﴿and in bringing you into being﴾, creating you ﴿in what you do not know﴾, of forms. Mujahid said: "In whatever form We wish."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: ﴿in what you do not know﴾ means: in the crops of birds that are in Barhut, as if they were swallows. Barhut is a valley in Yemen. al-Hasan said: ﴿and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾, meaning: We change your attributes and make you apes and swine, as We did to those before you.

al-Suddi said: We create you in other than your creation.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, the first creation, when you were nothing; ﴿so why do you not remember?﴾ That is, He who is capable of returning you is capable of originating you.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said concerning these meanings: although they are not rejected, what I hold regarding this verse, ﴿and We bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ and ﴿you have certainly known the first creation﴾, is this: I created you for resurrection after death in a manner you do not know, as I wish. That is because you knew the first creation, how it was in the wombs of mothers, and the second is not like that.

﴿Have you considered what you sow?﴾ That is, what you till the earth and work on it, and cast the seed. ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

Al-Husayn informed me: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayyat narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "None of you should say: 'I have sown,' but let him say: 'I have tilled.'" [203] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/218.]]

Abu Hurayra said: Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Have you considered what you till? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

﴿If We wished, We would make it crushed debris [hutaman], dry stalks, of no use for food or sustenance.﴾ He also said once: That is, a plant without wheat in it.

﴿So you would be left [fazaltum] ...﴾ The common recitation is with a fatha on the ẓa'. Abd Allah recited it with a kasra. The original is ẓallaltum, and one of the two lams was deleted for lightness. Whoever recites it with a fatha does so according to the original; whoever recites it with a kasra transfers the vowel of the deleted lam to the ẓa'.

﴿You would be left to fakihun [tafakkahun]﴾. Yaman said: You would regret your expenses, similar to: ﴿so he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾. [[Surat al-Kahf: 42.]]

Qatada: you would be amazed. Ikrima: you would blame one another. al-Hasan: you would regret the disobedience to Allah which made His punishment obligatory for you, so that what befell your crop befell you. Ibn Zayd: you would grieve. Ibn Kaysan: you would be sad.

He said: It is among the addad [words with opposite meanings]. The Arabs say: "tafakkahtu" means "I was made comfortable," and "tafakkahtu" also means "I was made sad."

al-Farra said: tafakkahun and tafakkanun are the same, and the nun is the dialect of Ukl [a tribe among the Arabs; it is also said: 'Adal'].

It is said: tafakkuh means speaking about what does not concern you, and from it comes "fukaha" for jesting.

﴿Indeed we are﴾: Asim, according to the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, recited with two hamzas. The rest recite it as a statement. The meaning of the verse: ﴿you would be left to fakihun﴾, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are burdened with debt [mughramun]﴾. Mujahid and Ikrima said: "We are obsessed with [it]." Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "We are punished, and al-gharam means punishment."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "Exposed to evil." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Destroyed."

al-Dahhak said: We have been burdened in our wealth, and what we spent became a debt upon us. Murra al-Hamadani: "Held to account."

﴿Rather, we are deprived [mahrumun]﴾: limited [mahdudun], [forbidden, mamnu'un] [[In the manuscript: "mumanna'un" with the nun doubled and both vowelled differently.]], cut off from provision; and the mahrum is the opposite of the one given provision.

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: "What prevents you from tilling?" They said: "Drought." He said: "Then do not do it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am the Sower: if I wish, I sow with water; if I wish, I sow with wind; if I wish, I sow with seed.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]] [204] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Have you considered what you till?﴾ and the verses.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds [al-muzn], or are We the senders?﴾ Al-muzn means the clouds; its singular is muzna.

The poet said:
"We are like rain-water: in our reservoir there is no ... and among us there is no one counted as a miser."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]]

﴿If We wished, We would make it ujaj [bitter]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: intensely salty. al-Hasan said: bitter and harsh.

﴿Why do you not give thanks?﴾

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle [tuwrun], striking it out of your flint? Is it you who produced its tree [shajaratuha] from which the fire is struck, which is the markh and the 'afar? Or are We the producers?﴾

﴿We made it﴾, that is, the fire of the world, ﴿a reminder [tadhkira] of the great Fire.﴾

Al-Husayn [...] Ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya, Abd al-Aziz ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part in seventy of the heat of Hell."

They said: "By Allah, it would be enough for us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts, each of which is like its heat." [[Sahih Muslim: 8/149.]] [205]

﴿And a provision [mata'an] for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾: for those who are benefitted, those who dwell in the open land, the qiy [and] the qawa, which is the barren, empty land far from settlement and inhabitants. It is said: "aqwat al-dar" when its inhabitants have left.

The poet said:
"It became desolate and bare, and the winds of the ... changed it, blowing dust hither and thither."
[[The hawj: the wind that blows steadily in its gusts; al-hābī: from the dust-storm (hibā') meaning it rose up; muwār: moving rapidly. The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/264.]]

al-Nabigha said:
"O Dariyya, at al-'Aliya and al-Sanad, it has become desolate there, and the long ages have passed over it."

This is the view of most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: ﴿for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾ means for the people who benefit, all of them, the travellers and those present, who are illuminated by it in darkness, warm themselves by it in cold, and benefit from it in cooking and baking, and by which we remember the Fire of Hell, and so we seek refuge with Allah from it.

al-Hasan said: "for the provision of the travellers, by which they reach their journeys, carrying it in bags and sacks."

al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: it means for the destitute, the needy who have no provision with them: a fire by which they kindle and bake. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: for the hungry.

The Arabs say: "aqwaytu mundhu kadha wa kadha," meaning I have not eaten anything.

Qutrub said: al-muqwi is one of the addad; it may mean poverty and it may mean wealth. It is said: "aqwa al-rajul" when his beasts became strong, and when his wealth became abundant.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.﴾

﴿So no! I swear [la uqsimu]﴾. Most exegetes said: its meaning is "I swear," and "la" is a redundant particle. This is confirmed by the recitation of Isa ibn Umar: (fa-la uqsimu) with clear hamza.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: its meaning is: "So it is not as they say," then he began the oath, saying: ﴿I swear by the setting-places of the stars﴾, meaning the stars of the Qur'an which were sent down ... their scattering and dispersal on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters differed about it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited (bi-mawqi') in the singular; others recited (bi-mawaqi') in the plural, and this is the preferred reading.

﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾, that is, this Book, and this is the place of the oath: ﴿indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ [hasin] [[an illegible word; the closest is what we have reconstructed.]], mighty and honoured.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: it is uncreated. It is also said: it was named "karim" because its ease overcomes its difficulty.

﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: protected, preserved with Allah, Glorified be He, safeguarded from the devils and from everything that defiles.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Husayn informed me: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Isa ibn al-Musawir narrated to us, and the wording is his, and they both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Isa ibn Musa Abu Muhammad and others narrated to us, from Urwa ibn Duwaym, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations﴾, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept and said: "O Prophet of Allah, a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later generations? We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a multitude of the later generations﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar and said: "O son of al-Khattab, Allah has sent down what you said, and He made it: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾."

Umar said: "We are content with our Lord and we affirm our Prophet."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From Adam to us is a multitude, and from me until [the Day of] Resurrection is a multitude, and it will not be completed except by the black men, shepherds of camels, who say: There is no god but Allah." [199] [[Asbab al-nuzul al-ayat (The Occasions of Revelation of the Verses): 270.]]

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: Umar ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning, we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers from their communities. A prophet would come with three from his community, and a prophet with a band from his community, and a prophet with a group from his community, and a prophet with a man from his community, and a prophet with no one from his community at all, until Moses came with a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they impressed me, so I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those of the Children of Israel who surround him.

I said: My Lord, then where is my community? It was said: Look to your right, and there, at the mountain slopes [[al-Zurab: the hills; a zurb is a stone whose base protrudes from a mountain or from hard ground (Kitab al-Ayn: 8/159). It was also said: they are small hills (al-Sihah: 1/174, under z-r-b).]] of Mecca, the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. Then it was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your community who will enter Paradise without reckoning."

He said: Ukasha ibn Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma, rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then another man rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "Ukasha has preceded you with this."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be among them; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. For I have seen people there, pressing upon one another in great numbers."

He said: I said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people who were born in Islam and continued to practise it until they died upon it. This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is not so, but they are those who do not seek cauterization by incantation, do not cauterize, and do not practise omens, and upon their Lord they rely." ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hope that those who follow me from my community will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. [200] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/420, where it reaches to his saying "Ukasha has preceded you with it"; Tarikh Jurjan: 373; al-Mustadrak: 4/578.]]

Abu al-Aliya, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations﴾ means those who preceded this community, and ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾ means from this community at the end of time.

What supports this is:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my community." [201] [[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/249.]]

﴿And those on the left—what of those on the left?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind﴾, a hot wind; ﴿and boiling water﴾, hot water; ﴿and a shade of black smoke﴾, a very black smoke. The Arabs say: "Aswad yahmum" when something is extremely black.

Qutrub recited:
"And what you drank in the valley of [Mecca] ... was sweet water, but like yahmum, my neighbour."

Ibn Buraydah said: al-Yahmum is a mountain in Hell, to whose shade the people of the Fire seek refuge. ﴿Neither cool﴾ but hot, because it is from the smoke of the blazing Hell. ﴿Nor pleasant﴾, nor sweet, according to al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan. A parallel: ﴿of every noble pair﴾. [[Surat al-Shu'ara: 7.]]

Muqatil: "good". Qatada: ﴿not cool﴾ as to its dwelling, ﴿nor pleasant﴾ as to its sight.

Al-Farra said: He makes "karim" follow everything of which he negates an act that carries blame. [[As in their saying: "This is not a spacious house, nor a pleasant one."]]

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Yahmum is one of the names of the Fire. al-Dahhak said: The Fire is black, its people are black, and everything in it is black.

The meaning of the verse: ﴿you would be left to fakihun﴾, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are burdened with debt [mughramun]﴾. Mujahid and Ikrima said: "We are obsessed with [it]." Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "We are punished, and al-gharam means punishment."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "Exposed to evil." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Destroyed."

al-Dahhak said: We have been burdened in our wealth, and what we spent became a debt upon us. Murra al-Hamadani: "Held to account."

﴿Rather, we are deprived [mahrumun]﴾: limited [mahdudun], [forbidden, mamnu'un] [[In the manuscript: "mumanna'un" with the nun doubled and both vowelled differently.]], cut off from provision; and the mahrum is the opposite of the one given provision.

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: "What prevents you from tilling?" They said: "Drought." He said: "Then do not do it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am the Sower: if I wish, I sow with water; if I wish, I sow with wind; if I wish, I sow with seed.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]] [204] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Have you considered what you till?﴾ and the verses.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds [al-muzn], or are We the senders?﴾ Al-muzn means the clouds; its singular is muzna.

The poet said:
"We are like rain-water: in our reservoir there is no ... and among us there is no one counted as a miser."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]]

﴿If We wished, We would make it ujaj [bitter]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: intensely salty. al-Hasan said: bitter and harsh.

﴿Why do you not give thanks?﴾

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle [tuwrun], striking it out of your flint? Is it you who produced its tree [shajaratuha] from which the fire is struck, which is the markh and the 'afar? Or are We the producers?﴾

﴿We made it﴾, that is, the fire of the world, ﴿a reminder [tadhkira] of the great Fire.﴾

Al-Husayn [...] Ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya, Abd al-Aziz ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part in seventy of the heat of Hell."

They said: "By Allah, it would be enough for us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts, each of which is like its heat." [[Sahih Muslim: 8/149.]] [205]

﴿And a provision [mata'an] for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾: for those who are benefitted, those who dwell in the open land, the qiy [and] the qawa, which is the barren, empty land far from settlement and inhabitants. It is said: "aqwat al-dar" when its inhabitants have left.

The poet said:
"It became desolate and bare, and the winds of the ... changed it, blowing dust hither and thither."
[[The hawj: the wind that blows steadily in its gusts; al-hābī: from the dust-storm (hibā') meaning it rose up; muwār: moving rapidly. The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/264.]]

al-Nabigha said:
"O Dariyya, at al-'Aliya and al-Sanad, it has become desolate there, and the long ages have passed over it."

This is the view of most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: ﴿for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾ means for the people who benefit, all of them, the travellers and those present, who are illuminated by it in darkness, warm themselves by it in cold, and benefit from it in cooking and baking, and by which we remember the Fire of Hell, and so we seek refuge with Allah from it.

al-Hasan said: "for the provision of the travellers, by which they reach their journeys, carrying it in bags and sacks."

al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: it means for the destitute, the needy who have no provision with them: a fire by which they kindle and bake. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: for the hungry.

The Arabs say: "aqwaytu mundhu kadha wa kadha," meaning I have not eaten anything.

Qutrub said: al-muqwi is one of the addad; it may mean poverty and it may mean wealth. It is said: "aqwa al-rajul" when his beasts became strong, and when his wealth became abundant.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.﴾

﴿So no! I swear [la uqsimu]﴾. Most exegetes said: its meaning is "I swear," and "la" is a redundant particle. This is confirmed by the recitation of Isa ibn Umar: (fa-la uqsimu) with clear hamza.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: its meaning is: "So it is not as they say," then he began the oath, saying: ﴿I swear by the setting-places of the stars﴾, meaning the stars of the Qur'an which were sent down ... their scattering and dispersal on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters differed about it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited (bi-mawqi') in the singular; others recited (bi-mawaqi') in the plural, and this is the preferred reading.

﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾, that is, this Book, and this is the place of the oath: ﴿indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ [hasin] [[an illegible word; the closest is what we have reconstructed.]], mighty and honoured.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: it is uncreated. It is also said: it was named "karim" because its ease overcomes its difficulty.

﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: protected, preserved with Allah, Glorified be He, safeguarded from the devils and from everything that defiles.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Husayn informed me: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Isa ibn al-Musawir narrated to us, and the wording is his, and they both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Isa ibn Musa Abu Muhammad and others narrated to us, from Urwa ibn Duwaym, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations﴾, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wept and said: "O Prophet of Allah, a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later generations? We believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, and few of us will be saved." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations, and a multitude of the later generations﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar and said: "O son of al-Khattab, Allah has sent down what you said, and He made it: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾."

Umar said: "We are content with our Lord and we affirm our Prophet."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From Adam to us is a multitude, and from me until [the Day of] Resurrection is a multitude, and it will not be completed except by the black men, shepherds of camels, who say: There is no god but Allah." [199] [[Asbab al-nuzul al-ayat (The Occasions of Revelation of the Verses): 270.]]

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: Umar ibn Abi Husayn narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we prolonged the conversation, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning, we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers from their communities. A prophet would come with three from his community, and a prophet with a band from his community, and a prophet with a group from his community, and a prophet with a man from his community, and a prophet with no one from his community at all, until Moses came with a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they impressed me, so I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those of the Children of Israel who surround him.

I said: My Lord, then where is my community? It was said: Look to your right, and there, at the mountain slopes [[al-Zurab: the hills; a zurb is a stone whose base protrudes from a mountain or from hard ground (Kitab al-Ayn: 8/159). It was also said: they are small hills (al-Sihah: 1/174, under z-r-b).]] of Mecca, the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men.

I said: My Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your community. Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content. Then it was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your community who will enter Paradise without reckoning."

He said: Ukasha ibn Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma, rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then another man rose and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them." He said: "Ukasha has preceded you with this."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be among them; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. For I have seen people there, pressing upon one another in great numbers."

He said: I said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people who were born in Islam and continued to practise it until they died upon it. This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is not so, but they are those who do not seek cauterization by incantation, do not cauterize, and do not practise omens, and upon their Lord they rely." ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hope that those who follow me from my community will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." We said "Allahu akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. [200] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/420, where it reaches to his saying "Ukasha has preceded you with it"; Tarikh Jurjan: 373; al-Mustadrak: 4/578.]]

Abu al-Aliya, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations﴾ means those who preceded this community, and ﴿and a few of the later generations﴾ means from this community at the end of time.

What supports this is:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿a multitude of the earlier generations and a multitude of the later generations﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my community." [201] [[Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/249.]]

﴿And those on the left—what of those on the left?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind﴾, a hot wind; ﴿and boiling water﴾, hot water; ﴿and a shade of black smoke﴾, a very black smoke. The Arabs say: "Aswad yahmum" when something is extremely black.

Qutrub recited:
"And what you drank in the valley of [Mecca] ... was sweet water, but like yahmum, my neighbour."

Ibn Buraydah said: al-Yahmum is a mountain in Hell, to whose shade the people of the Fire seek refuge. ﴿Neither cool﴾ but hot, because it is from the smoke of the blazing Hell. ﴿Nor pleasant﴾, nor sweet, according to al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan. A parallel: ﴿of every noble pair﴾. [[Surat al-Shu'ara: 7.]]

Muqatil: "good". Qatada: ﴿not cool﴾ as to its dwelling, ﴿nor pleasant﴾ as to its sight.

Al-Farra said: He makes "karim" follow everything of which he negates an act that carries blame. [[As in their saying: "This is not a spacious house, nor a pleasant one."]]

Ibn Kaysan said: al-Yahmum is one of the names of the Fire. al-Dahhak said: The Fire is black, its people are black, and everything in it is black.

﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent, living in luxury, and they used to persist in the great sin [al-hinth al-azim], that is, in the great wrong, which is shirk.

Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: They used to swear that there would be no resurrection, and that the idols were rivals to Allah, and they persisted in this, and that was their hinth.

﴿And they used to say: "When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be raised? And our forefathers, the earlier ones?" Say: "Indeed, the earlier and the later will all be gathered for the appointed time of a known day."﴾ Then it is said to them: ﴿Indeed, you, O astray, deniers, will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum, and fill your bellies with it, and drink upon it from the boiling water, drinking like the thirsty camels.﴾

The people of Medina, Asim (in the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal), Hamza, al-A'mash and Ayyub recited (shurba) with a ḍamma on the shin, and Abu Hatim chose this reading. The rest recited it with a fatha, and Abu Ubayd chose this.

It is transmitted from al-Kisa'i, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Juraij, that he said: I mentioned to Ja'far ibn Muhammad the recitation of the companions of Abd Allah: (shariba al-hiym) with a fatha on the shin. He said: "Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Budayl ibn Warqa al-Khuza'i to the people of Mina during the days of tashriq and said: 'Indeed, these are days of eating and drinking.'" [202] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/204; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/169.]]

It is said that it is with a fatha on the shin [and ... ] [[an illegible word.]], and both are good dialects.

The Arabs say: "shareba sharban, sharban, sharban" with two ḍammas.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: I heard the Arabs say: "sharibtu sharban," with a kasra on the shin.

As for (al-hiym), it means thirsty camels. Ikrima and Qatada said: it is a disease of camels, in which they are not satisfied [with it] [[In the manuscript: "ma'ha" (with it) rather than "ma'aha" as in the text.]] and never stop drinking until they die. This disease is called al-hiyam. It is said: a thirsty camel-stallion (hamal ahyam), a thirsty she-camel (naqa haymaa), and thirsty camels (ibil hiym).

Labid said:
"I passed over their traces with dishevelled [camels], and with swift, thirsty Mahri camels."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/215.]]

Al-Dahhak, Ibn Uyayna and Ibn Kaysan said: al-Hiym is the level sandy land.

﴿This is their nuzul [welcome/provision], their sustenance and what is prepared for them on the Day of Judgment.﴾ ﴿We created you, so why do you not affirm [the resurrection]?﴾ ﴿Have you considered what you emit [tumnun]?﴾ That is, what you pour into the wombs of the drops of semen.

Abu al-Sammak recited (tamnun) with a fatha on the ta, and both are dialects.

﴿Do you create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ ﴿We have decreed [qaddarna] among you death﴾. Mujahid, Humayd and Ibn Muhaysin recited (qadarna) with a lightened dal; the rest recited it with the shadda. So among you is one who lives until reaching old age, and among you is one who dies young, a child. ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾, unable to destroy you, ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾,

or replacing you with your likenesses, ﴿and in bringing you into being﴾, creating you ﴿in what you do not know﴾, of forms. Mujahid said: "In whatever form We wish."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: ﴿in what you do not know﴾ means: in the crops of birds that are in Barhut, as if they were swallows. Barhut is a valley in Yemen. al-Hasan said: ﴿and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾, meaning: We change your attributes and make you apes and swine, as We did to those before you.

al-Suddi said: We create you in other than your creation.

﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, the first creation, when you were nothing; ﴿so why do you not remember?﴾ That is, He who is capable of returning you is capable of originating you.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said concerning these meanings: although they are not rejected, what I hold regarding this verse, ﴿and We bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ and ﴿you have certainly known the first creation﴾, is this: I created you for resurrection after death in a manner you do not know, as I wish. That is because you knew the first creation, how it was in the wombs of mothers, and the second is not like that.

﴿Have you considered what you sow?﴾ That is, what you till the earth and work on it, and cast the seed. ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

Al-Husayn informed me: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayyat narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us: Makhlad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "None of you should say: 'I have sown,' but let him say: 'I have tilled.'" [203] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/218.]]

Abu Hurayra said: Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Have you considered what you till? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾

﴿If We wished, We would make it crushed debris [hutaman], dry stalks, of no use for food or sustenance.﴾ He also said once: That is, a plant without wheat in it.

﴿So you would be left [fazaltum] ...﴾ The common recitation is with a fatha on the ẓa'. Abd Allah recited it with a kasra. The original is ẓallaltum, and one of the two lams was deleted for lightness. Whoever recites it with a fatha does so according to the original; whoever recites it with a kasra transfers the vowel of the deleted lam to the ẓa'.

﴿You would be left to fakihun [tafakkahun]﴾. Yaman said: You would regret your expenses, similar to: ﴿so he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾. [[Surat al-Kahf: 42.]]

Qatada: you would be amazed. Ikrima: you would blame one another. al-Hasan: you would regret the disobedience to Allah which made His punishment obligatory for you, so that what befell your crop befell you. Ibn Zayd: you would grieve. Ibn Kaysan: you would be sad.

He said: It is among the addad [words with opposite meanings]. The Arabs say: "tafakkahtu" means "I was made comfortable," and "tafakkahtu" also means "I was made sad."

al-Farra said: tafakkahun and tafakkanun are the same, and the nun is the dialect of Ukl [a tribe among the Arabs; it is also said: 'Adal'].

It is said: tafakkuh means speaking about what does not concern you, and from it comes "fukaha" for jesting.

﴿Indeed we are﴾: Asim, according to the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, recited with two hamzas. The rest recite it as a statement. The meaning of the verse: ﴿you would be left to fakihun﴾, and you would say: ﴿Indeed we are burdened with debt [mughramun]﴾. Mujahid and Ikrima said: "We are obsessed with [it]." Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: "We are punished, and al-gharam means punishment."

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "Exposed to evil." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Destroyed."

al-Dahhak said: We have been burdened in our wealth, and what we spent became a debt upon us. Murra al-Hamadani: "Held to account."

﴿Rather, we are deprived [mahrumun]﴾: limited [mahdudun], [forbidden, mamnu'un] [[In the manuscript: "mumanna'un" with the nun doubled and both vowelled differently.]], cut off from provision; and the mahrum is the opposite of the one given provision.

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the land of the Ansar and said: "What prevents you from tilling?" They said: "Drought." He said: "Then do not do it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am the Sower: if I wish, I sow with water; if I wish, I sow with wind; if I wish, I sow with seed.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]] [204] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Have you considered what you till?﴾ and the verses.

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds [al-muzn], or are We the senders?﴾ Al-muzn means the clouds; its singular is muzna.

The poet said:
"We are like rain-water: in our reservoir there is no ... and among us there is no one counted as a miser."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/220.]]

﴿If We wished, We would make it ujaj [bitter]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: intensely salty. al-Hasan said: bitter and harsh.

﴿Why do you not give thanks?﴾

﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle [tuwrun], striking it out of your flint? Is it you who produced its tree [shajaratuha] from which the fire is struck, which is the markh and the 'afar? Or are We the producers?﴾

﴿We made it﴾, that is, the fire of the world, ﴿a reminder [tadhkira] of the great Fire.﴾

Al-Husayn [...] Ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdun narrated to us: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya, Abd al-Aziz ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part in seventy of the heat of Hell."

They said: "By Allah, it would be enough for us, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts, each of which is like its heat." [[Sahih Muslim: 8/149.]] [205]

﴿And a provision [mata'an] for the travellers [lil-muqwin]﴾: for those who are benefitted, those who dwell in the open land, the qiy [and] the qawa, which is the barren, empty land far from settlement and inhabitants. It is said: "aqwat al-dar" when its inhabitants have left.

The poet said:

al-Hasan said: "for the provision of the travellers, by which they reach their journeys, carrying it in bags and sacks."

al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: it means for the destitute, the needy who have no provision with them: a fire by which they kindle and bake. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: for the hungry.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.﴾

﴿So no! I swear [la uqsimu]﴾. Most exegetes said: its meaning is "I swear," and "la" is a redundant particle. This is confirmed by the recitation of Isa ibn Umar: (fa-la uqsimu) with clear hamza.

﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾, that is, this Book, and this is the place of the oath: ﴿indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ [hasin] [[an illegible word; the closest is what we have reconstructed.]], mighty and honoured.

To those on the right: a multitude of the earlier generations, ﴿and a multitude of the later generations﴾. "The earlier generations" means the past nations, and "the later generations" means the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).
