Some linguists said: "﴿مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ means: abandoning firmness in accepting this Qur'an and being careless about its command, and flattering the enemy and being soft toward him in place of what is required of opposing him. Its root is from softness and weakness."

Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat said:
"Firmness and strength are better than compromise... and the cowardly fear (?)"
[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/476, where it reads: "al-Ishfaq" instead of "al-Idhan."]

﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — your share and portion of the Qur'an — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.

Al-Hasan said: "In this verse: lost is the servant whose share of the Book of God is nothing but denial of it."

Others said: "This refers to seeking rain by the risings of stars (anwa')."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Ikrimah, related to us, Abu Zumayl related to us: Ibn Abbas told me, saying: "The people were given rain in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Some of the people have become thankful, and some have become disbelievers. They said: This is a mercy God has placed. And some of them said: The star-rising of such-and-such has spoken the truth.'" [207] [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/358, and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 12/153.]

He said: "Then this verse was revealed: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ up to ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾."

The explanation of this statement of Ibn Abbas regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse is what was narrated from him: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out on a journey, and they stopped, and they were struck by thirst while they had no water. They mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Do you see? If I supplicate for you and you are given water, perhaps you will say: We were watered by the rain of such-and-such star-rising." [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat: 271.] [208]

They said: "O Messenger of God, this is not the time of the star-risings."

He said: So he prayed two rak'as and supplicated to his Lord. A wind blew, then a cloud arose, and they were rained upon until the valleys flowed and they filled their water-skins. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rode and passed by a man who was scooping water with a bowl, saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of so-and-so," and he did not say: "This is from the provision of God." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — that is, your thanks to God for His provision to you — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ — by denying the blessing and saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of such-and-such."

This is like the saying of one who says: "I made giving to you an offense on your part toward me, and I made the thanks for my honoring you that you took me as an enemy." So the meaning of the verse is: "And you make the thanks for your provision," so the genitive (mudaf) is omitted and the genitive-attached (mudaf ilayhi) is put in its place, like His saying ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82] and similar.

The poet said:
"The people's thanks, at the time of favors, were like the sincere she-camels' drooping eyes."

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad related to us: my father related to us: Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim, from Ali, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: "And you make your thanks that you are denying." (وتجعلون شكركم أنكم تكذبون)

And al-Haytham mentioned, from Adi, that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah: "ma razaqa Fulan," meaning "ma shakara" (what so-and-so thanked). [Cf. Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/294, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/178.]

Aqil and al-Mu'afi informed me: Muhammad ibn Jarir related to me: Yunus related to me: Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, Glorified and Exalted, indeed morns His servants with a blessing or evens them with it, so a people become disbelievers in the morning, saying: 'We were rained upon by the star-rising of such-and-such.'" [209] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/164.]

Muhammad said: "I mentioned this hadith to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: 'We too have heard from Abu Hurayrah. And one who witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, informed me that he was seeking rain, and when he sought rain he turned to al-'Abbas and said: "O uncle of the Messenger of God, how much of the star-rising of the Pleiades remains?" He said: "The scholars claim that it remains visible on the horizon for seven [nights] after its setting." He said: So the seventh had not passed before they were rained upon.'" [210] [Musnad al-Humaydi: 2/432, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271.]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd related to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Talhah, from Abdullah ibn Muhayrih, who said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik summoned him and said: "If only you had learned the science of the stars, you would have increased in your knowledge."

He said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The thing I fear most for my nation is three: the injustice of rulers, denial of divine decree, and belief in the stars.'" [Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/47, no. 279, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 6/15, no. 14632, with slight variation.] [211]

Then He addressed them with an address of warning and dread, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ — why not? — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ — meaning the soul — ﴿الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ — at its departure from the body. The soul is omitted because the context indicates it.

Like the saying of the poet:
"O my mother, wealth does not avail against poverty, when the death-rattle comes upon one one day and the chest is constricted."

﴿وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — at my command and my authority.

Ibn Abbas said: "He means: those present at the dying person from among his family, looking at him, when his soul will leave."

Al-Farra' said: "This is known from the speech of the Arabs: that they address the group with the verb, as if they were his family and companions, while the intended is some of them, whether absent or present. They say: 'You killed so-and-so,' while the killer is one of them."

They also say to the people of the mosque when they harm a man by crowding: "Fear God, for you are harming the Muslims." ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ — by power and knowledge — and you have no power to repel anything from him.

Amir ibn Abd Qays said: "I never looked at anything without seeing God, Glorified is He, nearer to me than it."

Some said: "He meant: And Our messengers who take him in death."

﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾. ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾ — owned (not subject to command), and held accountable and recompensed.

If it is said: "Where is the answer to His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ and His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾?"

We say: Al-Farra' said: "Both have been answered with one answer, which is His saying ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾. The Arabs sometimes repeat two particles while their meaning is one, and this is of that type. And of it is His saying ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدىً فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدايَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, where both have one answer, though they are two clauses. And of it is His saying ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ﴾." [Surah Al 'Imran: 188.]

It was also said: the verse has an inversion and a reordering, its meaning being: ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ — that is, you return the soul of this dead man to his body — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ﴾. Then He mentioned the classes of creation at death and at resurrection, and explained their ranks, saying: ﴿فَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ — those who are foremost — ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ra', in the sense that his spirit leaves amid basil (rayhan). Al-Hasan said this.

Qatadah said: "The rawh is mercy." It was also said: the meaning is: "then life and continuance for them." It is mentioned that this was the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: Abu Ubayd informed us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Abu Hammad al-Khurasani, from Badil ibn Maysarah, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to read this word: (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

And with his chain, from Abu Ubayd: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun. And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad informed us: my father related to us: al-Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim: Badil ibn Maysarah informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

The others read it with a fatha on the ra'.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "Ease (farahah)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Joy (farah)." Al-Dahhak: "Forgiveness and mercy."

﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: "A place of rest (mustarah)." Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Provision (rizq)." Muqatil said: "It is in the language of Himyar; it is said: 'I went out seeking the rayhan of God,' meaning His provision."

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym and Ibn Zayd said: "(فَرَوْحٌ) at death, (وَرَيْحانٌ) which is stored up for him in the Hereafter."

Others said: "It is the well-known basil that is smelled."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "None of the foremost departs from the world until a sprig of the basil of Paradise is brought to him, and he smells it, and then he dies."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/276.]

﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "The rawh is deliverance from the Fire, and the rayhan is entering the abode of permanence."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "The rawh is rest in the grave, and the rayhan is entering Paradise."

Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The rawh is safety, and the rayhan is honor."

Poetry: [This is how it appears in the manuscript, and it is not in fact poetry.] "The rawh is embracing virgin maidens, and the rayhan is the company of the righteous; the 'breath' (bahran) of the rawh is the unveiling of the veil, and the rayhan is contemplation and meeting."

It was also said: "The rawh is rest, and the rayhan is deliverance from calamity." It was said: "The rawh is death as a martyr, and the rayhan is the call of happiness." It was said: "The rawh is the removal of distresses, and the rayhan is the forgiveness of sins." It was said: "The rawh is steadfastness upon faith, and the rayhan is attaining security and safety."

It was said: "The rawh is abundance (fadlah), and the rayhan is [fadalah]." [In the manuscript it is fadlah in both places.] It was said: "The rawh is lightening of the reckoning, and the rayhan is multiplication of reward."

It was said: "The rawh is pardon without reproach, and the rayhan is provision without reckoning."

It is said: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾ is for the foremost, ﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ for the moderate, and ﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾ for the seekers.

It was said: "The rawh is for their spirits, the rayhan for their hearts, the Garden for their bodies, and the Truth for their inner secrets."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ — ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ﴾ — the nominative is in the sense of: "For you there is peace," and it is "peace for you," i.e., safety for you, O Muhammad, from them, so do not be concerned for them, for they have been saved from the punishment of God.

Al-Farra' said: "It is certain for you that they are among the companions of the right." Or it is said to the companion of the right: "It is certain for you that you are among the companions of the right." It was also said: "Then peace upon you from the companions of the right."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ — those who are the people of the left hand — ﴿فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ — ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ — and entry into the Fire. ﴿إِنَّ هذا الذي ذكروا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾ — that is, the true certainty, and He attributed it to Himself, and we have mentioned its parallels.

Qatadah said regarding this verse: "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, does not leave any person until He makes him stand upon certainty concerning this Qur'an. As for the believer, he attains certainty in this world, and that benefits him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he attains certainty on the Day of Resurrection, when it will not benefit him."

﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — so pray, with the remembrance and mention of your Lord — ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾. It was also said: "Remember the name of your Lord, the Mighty, and glorify Him."

Al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Katib narrated to us: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, from his paternal uncle, who is Iyas ibn Amir, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Place it in your ruku' (bowing)." And when ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Place it in your sujud (prostration)." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/155.] [212]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Muqri informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim al-Nabil informed us: al-Hawsi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Abu Bilal, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Musabbihat before he slept, and would say: "Indeed, in them there is a verse better than a thousand verses." [213] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/128.]

He said: By the Musabbihat he means: al-Hadid, al-Hashr, al-Saff, al-Jumu'ah, and al-Taghabun.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ — that is, that Book — ﴿إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — purified from sins — and they are the angels.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Tarkhan related to us: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abdus informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Mahfuz informed us: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us: Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Rabi', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels who are in the heavens."

Abu al-Aliyah and Ibn Zayd said: "It is not you who are the people of sins. Rather, they are those who have been purified from sins, like the angelic messengers and the human messengers. Gabriel, who brings it down, is purified, and the messengers to whom he brings it are purified."

Ibn Abbas said: "[Purified] from polytheism." Ikrimah said: "They are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel."

Qatadah said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ عند الله إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — with God, only the purified touch it. As for in this world, it is touched by the impure disbeliever and the abominable hypocrite."

Habban, from al-Kalbi: "They are the noble scribe-angels, the righteous." Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from him: "No one recites it except the monotheists."

Ikrimah said: "Ibn Abbas used to forbid that the Jews and Christians be enabled to recite the Qur'an."

Al-Farra': "They do not find its taste and benefit except those who believe in it."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: "No one knows its exegesis and interpretation except those whom God has purified from polytheism and hypocrisy."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "Only the fortunate are granted success in acting upon it."

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata': "No one understands the realities of the Qur'an except one whose inner self has been purified of impurities in the presence of the lights."

Junayd: "They are those whose inner selves have been purified from everything other than God."

Some people said: "Its meaning is: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — from minor and major ritual impurities and from filth." They returned the pronoun in His saying ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ to the Qur'an.

They said: "He meant by the Qur'an the physical copy (mushaf), calling it 'Qur'an' by close association and extension, like the sound report that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade that the Qur'an be taken to the land of the enemy." [See Muwatta' of Malik: 2/446, and Sahih Muslim: 6/30.]

They said: "The apparent wording of the verse is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَالْمُطَلَّقاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ and similar verses." They cited this verse as proof for prohibiting the one in a state of major impurity (junub), the menstruating woman, and the one in a state of minor impurity (muhdith) from touching and carrying the mushaf. They said: "It is not permissible for anyone to carry the mushaf or touch it until he is in a state that makes prayer permissible for him." He said: "This is the position of the majority of jurists, except that Abu Hanifah does not prohibit carrying it by its cover or touching it with an intervening barrier. The preferred view is that it is prohibited, because when he carries it in its leather covering, he is carrying it through an intervening barrier, and even so it is prohibited."

Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Dawud ibn Ali held that there is no harm in carrying the mushaf and touching it in any state whatsoever, whether one is pure or impure, believer or unbeliever. However, Dawud said: "It is not permissible for a polytheist to carry the mushaf."

The evidence that it is not carried or touched except by one who is pure is what Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jarm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to Yemen, he wrote in his letter that none should carry the mushaf or touch it except one who is pure.

And Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar narrated from his father that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not touch the Qur'an except while you are pure." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/615.] [206]

And because the Companions unanimously agreed upon it.

It was narrated that 'Ali was asked: "Does one in a state of minor impurity touch the mushaf?" He said: "No."

It was narrated that Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was reading from the mushaf, and he put his hand in and scratched his penis, so his father took the mushaf from his hand and said: "Stand up, perform ablution, then take it." There was no dissenter among the Companions regarding these two.

'Ata' said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — only one who is in ablution may turn the pages of the mushaf."

Those who permitted it cited the letter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Caesar, which contained: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate... ﴿قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ تَعالَوْا إِلى كَلِمَةٍ سَواءٍ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾," the verse. [Surah Al 'Imran: 64.]

The jurists permitted it when there is a necessity or an excuse compels one to it. As for children, our companions (the Shafi'is) have two opinions:

One: they are prohibited from it, like adults.

The second: they are not prohibited, for two reasons. The first: if children were prohibited from it, it would lead to their not being taught the Qur'an, not learning it, and not memorizing it, because the time for learning and memorizing it is in childhood.

The second: although a child has purity, it is not complete, because his intention is not valid. So if it is permissible for him to carry it in incomplete purity, it is permissible for him to carry it while in a state of minor impurity. And God knows best.

﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ — that is, sent down — ﴿مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾. The sent-down thing is called "a sending down" (tanzil) by the breadth of the language, just as you say "the decreed" for "a decree" and "the created" for "a creation," and "this dirham was minted by the ruler" and "weighed seven [mithqals]," and similar expressions.

﴿أَفَبِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Deniers."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Disbelievers." Its parallel is His saying ﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾. [Surah al-Qalam: 9.]

Ibn Kaysan said: "The mudhin (one who compromises) is one who does not do what is due upon him, and repels it with excuses."

The historian said: "The mudhin is the hypocrite who softens his side to conceal his disbelief. Idhan and dahana are the same, and its root is from oil (dahn)." Mujahid said: "You want to flatter them in it and incline toward them."

Some linguists said: "﴿مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ means: abandoning firmness in accepting this Qur'an and being careless about its command, and flattering the enemy and being soft toward him in place of what is required of opposing him. Its root is from softness and weakness."

Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat said:
"Firmness and strength are better than compromise... and the cowardly fear (?)"
[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/476, where it reads: "al-Ishfaq" instead of "al-Idhan."]

﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — your share and portion of the Qur'an — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.

Al-Hasan said: "In this verse: lost is the servant whose share of the Book of God is nothing but denial of it."

Others said: "This refers to seeking rain by the risings of stars (anwa')."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Ikrimah, related to us, Abu Zumayl related to us: Ibn Abbas told me, saying: "The people were given rain in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Some of the people have become thankful, and some have become disbelievers. They said: This is a mercy God has placed. And some of them said: The star-rising of such-and-such has spoken the truth.'" [207] [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/358, and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 12/153.]

He said: "Then this verse was revealed: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ up to ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾."

The explanation of this statement of Ibn Abbas regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse is what was narrated from him: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out on a journey, and they stopped, and they were struck by thirst while they had no water. They mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Do you see? If I supplicate for you and you are given water, perhaps you will say: We were watered by the rain of such-and-such star-rising." [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat: 271.] [208]

They said: "O Messenger of God, this is not the time of the star-risings."

He said: So he prayed two rak'as and supplicated to his Lord. A wind blew, then a cloud arose, and they were rained upon until the valleys flowed and they filled their water-skins. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rode and passed by a man who was scooping water with a bowl, saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of so-and-so," and he did not say: "This is from the provision of God." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — that is, your thanks to God for His provision to you — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ — by denying the blessing and saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of such-and-such."

This is like the saying of one who says: "I made giving to you an offense on your part toward me, and I made the thanks for my honoring you that you took me as an enemy." So the meaning of the verse is: "And you make the thanks for your provision," so the genitive (mudaf) is omitted and the genitive-attached (mudaf ilayhi) is put in its place, like His saying ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82] and similar.

The poet said:
"The people's thanks, at the time of favors, were like the sincere she-camels' drooping eyes."

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad related to us: my father related to us: Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim, from Ali, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: "And you make your thanks that you are denying." (وتجعلون شكركم أنكم تكذبون)

And al-Haytham mentioned, from Adi, that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah: "ma razaqa Fulan," meaning "ma shakara" (what so-and-so thanked). [Cf. Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/294, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/178.]

Aqil and al-Mu'afi informed me: Muhammad ibn Jarir related to me: Yunus related to me: Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, Glorified and Exalted, indeed morns His servants with a blessing or evens them with it, so a people become disbelievers in the morning, saying: 'We were rained upon by the star-rising of such-and-such.'" [209] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/164.]

Muhammad said: "I mentioned this hadith to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: 'We too have heard from Abu Hurayrah. And one who witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, informed me that he was seeking rain, and when he sought rain he turned to al-'Abbas and said: "O uncle of the Messenger of God, how much of the star-rising of the Pleiades remains?" He said: "The scholars claim that it remains visible on the horizon for seven [nights] after its setting." He said: So the seventh had not passed before they were rained upon.'" [210] [Musnad al-Humaydi: 2/432, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271.]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd related to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Talhah, from Abdullah ibn Muhayrih, who said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik summoned him and said: "If only you had learned the science of the stars, you would have increased in your knowledge."

He said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The thing I fear most for my nation is three: the injustice of rulers, denial of divine decree, and belief in the stars.'" [Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/47, no. 279, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 6/15, no. 14632, with slight variation.] [211]

Then He addressed them with an address of warning and dread, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ — why not? — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ — meaning the soul — ﴿الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ — at its departure from the body. The soul is omitted because the context indicates it.

Like the saying of the poet:
"O my mother, wealth does not avail against poverty, when the death-rattle comes upon one one day and the chest is constricted."

﴿وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — at my command and my authority.

Ibn Abbas said: "He means: those present at the dying person from among his family, looking at him, when his soul will leave."

Al-Farra' said: "This is known from the speech of the Arabs: that they address the group with the verb, as if they were his family and companions, while the intended is some of them, whether absent or present. They say: 'You killed so-and-so,' while the killer is one of them."

They also say to the people of the mosque when they harm a man by crowding: "Fear God, for you are harming the Muslims." ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ — by power and knowledge — and you have no power to repel anything from him.

Amir ibn Abd Qays said: "I never looked at anything without seeing God, Glorified is He, nearer to me than it."

Some said: "He meant: And Our messengers who take him in death."

﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾. ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾ — owned (not subject to command), and held accountable and recompensed.

If it is said: "Where is the answer to His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ and His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾?"

We say: Al-Farra' said: "Both have been answered with one answer, which is His saying ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾. The Arabs sometimes repeat two particles while their meaning is one, and this is of that type. And of it is His saying ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدىً فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدايَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, where both have one answer, though they are two clauses. And of it is His saying ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ﴾." [Surah Al 'Imran: 188.]

It was also said: the verse has an inversion and a reordering, its meaning being: ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ — that is, you return the soul of this dead man to his body — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ﴾. Then He mentioned the classes of creation at death and at resurrection, and explained their ranks, saying: ﴿فَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ — those who are foremost — ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ra', in the sense that his spirit leaves amid basil (rayhan). Al-Hasan said this.

Qatadah said: "The rawh is mercy." It was also said: the meaning is: "then life and continuance for them." It is mentioned that this was the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: Abu Ubayd informed us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Abu Hammad al-Khurasani, from Badil ibn Maysarah, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to read this word: (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

And with his chain, from Abu Ubayd: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun. And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad informed us: my father related to us: al-Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim: Badil ibn Maysarah informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

The others read it with a fatha on the ra'.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "Ease (farahah)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Joy (farah)." Al-Dahhak: "Forgiveness and mercy."

﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: "A place of rest (mustarah)." Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Provision (rizq)." Muqatil said: "It is in the language of Himyar; it is said: 'I went out seeking the rayhan of God,' meaning His provision."

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym and Ibn Zayd said: "(فَرَوْحٌ) at death, (وَرَيْحانٌ) which is stored up for him in the Hereafter."

Others said: "It is the well-known basil that is smelled."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "None of the foremost departs from the world until a sprig of the basil of Paradise is brought to him, and he smells it, and then he dies."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/276.]

﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "The rawh is deliverance from the Fire, and the rayhan is entering the abode of permanence."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "The rawh is rest in the grave, and the rayhan is entering Paradise."

Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The rawh is safety, and the rayhan is honor."

Poetry: [This is how it appears in the manuscript, and it is not in fact poetry.] "The rawh is embracing virgin maidens, and the rayhan is the company of the righteous; the 'breath' (bahran) of the rawh is the unveiling of the veil, and the rayhan is contemplation and meeting."

It was also said: "The rawh is rest, and the rayhan is deliverance from calamity." It was said: "The rawh is death as a martyr, and the rayhan is the call of happiness." It was said: "The rawh is the removal of distresses, and the rayhan is the forgiveness of sins." It was said: "The rawh is steadfastness upon faith, and the rayhan is attaining security and safety."

It was said: "The rawh is abundance (fadlah), and the rayhan is [fadalah]." [In the manuscript it is fadlah in both places.] It was said: "The rawh is lightening of the reckoning, and the rayhan is multiplication of reward."

It was said: "The rawh is pardon without reproach, and the rayhan is provision without reckoning."

It is said: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾ is for the foremost, ﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ for the moderate, and ﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾ for the seekers.

It was said: "The rawh is for their spirits, the rayhan for their hearts, the Garden for their bodies, and the Truth for their inner secrets."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ — ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ﴾ — the nominative is in the sense of: "For you there is peace," and it is "peace for you," i.e., safety for you, O Muhammad, from them, so do not be concerned for them, for they have been saved from the punishment of God.

Al-Farra' said: "It is certain for you that they are among the companions of the right." Or it is said to the companion of the right: "It is certain for you that you are among the companions of the right." It was also said: "Then peace upon you from the companions of the right."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ — those who are the people of the left hand — ﴿فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ — ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ — and entry into the Fire. ﴿إِنَّ هذا الذي ذكروا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾ — that is, the true certainty, and He attributed it to Himself, and we have mentioned its parallels.

Qatadah said regarding this verse: "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, does not leave any person until He makes him stand upon certainty concerning this Qur'an. As for the believer, he attains certainty in this world, and that benefits him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he attains certainty on the Day of Resurrection, when it will not benefit him."

﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — so pray, with the remembrance and mention of your Lord — ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾. It was also said: "Remember the name of your Lord, the Mighty, and glorify Him."

Al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Katib narrated to us: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, from his paternal uncle, who is Iyas ibn Amir, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Place it in your ruku' (bowing)." And when ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Place it in your sujud (prostration)." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/155.] [212]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Muqri informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim al-Nabil informed us: al-Hawsi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Abu Bilal, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Musabbihat before he slept, and would say: "Indeed, in them there is a verse better than a thousand verses." [213] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/128.]

He said: By the Musabbihat he means: al-Hadid, al-Hashr, al-Saff, al-Jumu'ah, and al-Taghabun.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ — that is, that Book — ﴿إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — purified from sins — and they are the angels.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Tarkhan related to us: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abdus informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Mahfuz informed us: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us: Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Rabi', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels who are in the heavens."

Abu al-Aliyah and Ibn Zayd said: "It is not you who are the people of sins. Rather, they are those who have been purified from sins, like the angelic messengers and the human messengers. Gabriel, who brings it down, is purified, and the messengers to whom he brings it are purified."

Ibn Abbas said: "[Purified] from polytheism." Ikrimah said: "They are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel."

Qatadah said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ عند الله إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — with God, only the purified touch it. As for in this world, it is touched by the impure disbeliever and the abominable hypocrite."

Habban, from al-Kalbi: "They are the noble scribe-angels, the righteous." Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from him: "No one recites it except the monotheists."

Ikrimah said: "Ibn Abbas used to forbid that the Jews and Christians be enabled to recite the Qur'an."

Al-Farra': "They do not find its taste and benefit except those who believe in it."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: "No one knows its exegesis and interpretation except those whom God has purified from polytheism and hypocrisy."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "Only the fortunate are granted success in acting upon it."

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata': "No one understands the realities of the Qur'an except one whose inner self has been purified of impurities in the presence of the lights."

Junayd: "They are those whose inner selves have been purified from everything other than God."

Some people said: "Its meaning is: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — from minor and major ritual impurities and from filth." They returned the pronoun in His saying ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ to the Qur'an.

They said: "He meant by the Qur'an the physical copy (mushaf), calling it 'Qur'an' by close association and extension, like the sound report that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade that the Qur'an be taken to the land of the enemy." [See Muwatta' of Malik: 2/446, and Sahih Muslim: 6/30.]

They said: "The apparent wording of the verse is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَالْمُطَلَّقاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ and similar verses." They cited this verse as proof for prohibiting the one in a state of major impurity (junub), the menstruating woman, and the one in a state of minor impurity (muhdith) from touching and carrying the mushaf. They said: "It is not permissible for anyone to carry the mushaf or touch it until he is in a state that makes prayer permissible for him." He said: "This is the position of the majority of jurists, except that Abu Hanifah does not prohibit carrying it by its cover or touching it with an intervening barrier. The preferred view is that it is prohibited, because when he carries it in its leather covering, he is carrying it through an intervening barrier, and even so it is prohibited."

Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Dawud ibn Ali held that there is no harm in carrying the mushaf and touching it in any state whatsoever, whether one is pure or impure, believer or unbeliever. However, Dawud said: "It is not permissible for a polytheist to carry the mushaf."

The evidence that it is not carried or touched except by one who is pure is what Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jarm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to Yemen, he wrote in his letter that none should carry the mushaf or touch it except one who is pure.

And Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar narrated from his father that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not touch the Qur'an except while you are pure." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/615.] [206]

And because the Companions unanimously agreed upon it.

It was narrated that 'Ali was asked: "Does one in a state of minor impurity touch the mushaf?" He said: "No."

It was narrated that Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was reading from the mushaf, and he put his hand in and scratched his penis, so his father took the mushaf from his hand and said: "Stand up, perform ablution, then take it." There was no dissenter among the Companions regarding these two.

'Ata' said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — only one who is in ablution may turn the pages of the mushaf."

Those who permitted it cited the letter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Caesar, which contained: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate... ﴿قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ تَعالَوْا إِلى كَلِمَةٍ سَواءٍ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾," the verse. [Surah Al 'Imran: 64.]

The jurists permitted it when there is a necessity or an excuse compels one to it. As for children, our companions (the Shafi'is) have two opinions:

One: they are prohibited from it, like adults.

The second: they are not prohibited, for two reasons. The first: if children were prohibited from it, it would lead to their not being taught the Qur'an, not learning it, and not memorizing it, because the time for learning and memorizing it is in childhood.

The second: although a child has purity, it is not complete, because his intention is not valid. So if it is permissible for him to carry it in incomplete purity, it is permissible for him to carry it while in a state of minor impurity. And God knows best.

﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ — that is, sent down — ﴿مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾. The sent-down thing is called "a sending down" (tanzil) by the breadth of the language, just as you say "the decreed" for "a decree" and "the created" for "a creation," and "this dirham was minted by the ruler" and "weighed seven [mithqals]," and similar expressions.

﴿أَفَبِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Deniers."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Disbelievers." Its parallel is His saying ﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾. [Surah al-Qalam: 9.]

Ibn Kaysan said: "The mudhin (one who compromises) is one who does not do what is due upon him, and repels it with excuses."

The historian said: "The mudhin is the hypocrite who softens his side to conceal his disbelief. Idhan and dahana are the same, and its root is from oil (dahn)." Mujahid said: "You want to flatter them in it and incline toward them."

Some linguists said: "﴿مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ means: abandoning firmness in accepting this Qur'an and being careless about its command, and flattering the enemy and being soft toward him in place of what is required of opposing him. Its root is from softness and weakness."

Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat said:
"Firmness and strength are better than compromise... and the cowardly fear (?)"
[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/476, where it reads: "al-Ishfaq" instead of "al-Idhan."]

﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — your share and portion of the Qur'an — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.

Al-Hasan said: "In this verse: lost is the servant whose share of the Book of God is nothing but denial of it."

Others said: "This refers to seeking rain by the risings of stars (anwa')."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Ikrimah, related to us, Abu Zumayl related to us: Ibn Abbas told me, saying: "The people were given rain in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Some of the people have become thankful, and some have become disbelievers. They said: This is a mercy God has placed. And some of them said: The star-rising of such-and-such has spoken the truth.'" [207] [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/358, and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 12/153.]

He said: "Then this verse was revealed: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ up to ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾."

The explanation of this statement of Ibn Abbas regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse is what was narrated from him: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out on a journey, and they stopped, and they were struck by thirst while they had no water. They mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Do you see? If I supplicate for you and you are given water, perhaps you will say: We were watered by the rain of such-and-such star-rising." [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat: 271.] [208]

They said: "O Messenger of God, this is not the time of the star-risings."

He said: So he prayed two rak'as and supplicated to his Lord. A wind blew, then a cloud arose, and they were rained upon until the valleys flowed and they filled their water-skins. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rode and passed by a man who was scooping water with a bowl, saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of so-and-so," and he did not say: "This is from the provision of God." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — that is, your thanks to God for His provision to you — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ — by denying the blessing and saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of such-and-such."

This is like the saying of one who says: "I made giving to you an offense on your part toward me, and I made the thanks for my honoring you that you took me as an enemy." So the meaning of the verse is: "And you make the thanks for your provision," so the genitive (mudaf) is omitted and the genitive-attached (mudaf ilayhi) is put in its place, like His saying ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82] and similar.

The poet said:
"The people's thanks, at the time of favors, were like the sincere she-camels' drooping eyes."

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad related to us: my father related to us: Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim, from Ali, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: "And you make your thanks that you are denying." (وتجعلون شكركم أنكم تكذبون)

And al-Haytham mentioned, from Adi, that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah: "ma razaqa Fulan," meaning "ma shakara" (what so-and-so thanked). [Cf. Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/294, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/178.]

Aqil and al-Mu'afi informed me: Muhammad ibn Jarir related to me: Yunus related to me: Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, Glorified and Exalted, indeed morns His servants with a blessing or evens them with it, so a people become disbelievers in the morning, saying: 'We were rained upon by the star-rising of such-and-such.'" [209] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/164.]

Muhammad said: "I mentioned this hadith to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: 'We too have heard from Abu Hurayrah. And one who witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, informed me that he was seeking rain, and when he sought rain he turned to al-'Abbas and said: "O uncle of the Messenger of God, how much of the star-rising of the Pleiades remains?" He said: "The scholars claim that it remains visible on the horizon for seven [nights] after its setting." He said: So the seventh had not passed before they were rained upon.'" [210] [Musnad al-Humaydi: 2/432, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271.]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd related to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Talhah, from Abdullah ibn Muhayrih, who said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik summoned him and said: "If only you had learned the science of the stars, you would have increased in your knowledge."

He said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The thing I fear most for my nation is three: the injustice of rulers, denial of divine decree, and belief in the stars.'" [Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/47, no. 279, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 6/15, no. 14632, with slight variation.] [211]

Then He addressed them with an address of warning and dread, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ — why not? — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ — meaning the soul — ﴿الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ — at its departure from the body. The soul is omitted because the context indicates it.

Like the saying of the poet:
"O my mother, wealth does not avail against poverty, when the death-rattle comes upon one one day and the chest is constricted."

﴿وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — at my command and my authority.

Ibn Abbas said: "He means: those present at the dying person from among his family, looking at him, when his soul will leave."

Al-Farra' said: "This is known from the speech of the Arabs: that they address the group with the verb, as if they were his family and companions, while the intended is some of them, whether absent or present. They say: 'You killed so-and-so,' while the killer is one of them."

They also say to the people of the mosque when they harm a man by crowding: "Fear God, for you are harming the Muslims." ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ — by power and knowledge — and you have no power to repel anything from him.

Amir ibn Abd Qays said: "I never looked at anything without seeing God, Glorified is He, nearer to me than it."

Some said: "He meant: And Our messengers who take him in death."

﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾. ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾ — owned (not subject to command), and held accountable and recompensed.

If it is said: "Where is the answer to His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ and His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾?"

We say: Al-Farra' said: "Both have been answered with one answer, which is His saying ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾. The Arabs sometimes repeat two particles while their meaning is one, and this is of that type. And of it is His saying ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدىً فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدايَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, where both have one answer, though they are two clauses. And of it is His saying ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ﴾." [Surah Al 'Imran: 188.]

It was also said: the verse has an inversion and a reordering, its meaning being: ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ — that is, you return the soul of this dead man to his body — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ﴾. Then He mentioned the classes of creation at death and at resurrection, and explained their ranks, saying: ﴿فَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ — those who are foremost — ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ra', in the sense that his spirit leaves amid basil (rayhan). Al-Hasan said this.

Qatadah said: "The rawh is mercy." It was also said: the meaning is: "then life and continuance for them." It is mentioned that this was the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: Abu Ubayd informed us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Abu Hammad al-Khurasani, from Badil ibn Maysarah, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to read this word: (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

And with his chain, from Abu Ubayd: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun. And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad informed us: my father related to us: al-Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim: Badil ibn Maysarah informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

The others read it with a fatha on the ra'.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "Ease (farahah)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Joy (farah)." Al-Dahhak: "Forgiveness and mercy."

﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: "A place of rest (mustarah)." Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Provision (rizq)." Muqatil said: "It is in the language of Himyar; it is said: 'I went out seeking the rayhan of God,' meaning His provision."

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym and Ibn Zayd said: "(فَرَوْحٌ) at death, (وَرَيْحانٌ) which is stored up for him in the Hereafter."

Others said: "It is the well-known basil that is smelled."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "None of the foremost departs from the world until a sprig of the basil of Paradise is brought to him, and he smells it, and then he dies."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/276.]

﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "The rawh is deliverance from the Fire, and the rayhan is entering the abode of permanence."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "The rawh is rest in the grave, and the rayhan is entering Paradise."

Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The rawh is safety, and the rayhan is honor."

Poetry: [This is how it appears in the manuscript, and it is not in fact poetry.] "The rawh is embracing virgin maidens, and the rayhan is the company of the righteous; the 'breath' (bahran) of the rawh is the unveiling of the veil, and the rayhan is contemplation and meeting."

It was also said: "The rawh is rest, and the rayhan is deliverance from calamity." It was said: "The rawh is death as a martyr, and the rayhan is the call of happiness." It was said: "The rawh is the removal of distresses, and the rayhan is the forgiveness of sins." It was said: "The rawh is steadfastness upon faith, and the rayhan is attaining security and safety."

It was said: "The rawh is abundance (fadlah), and the rayhan is [fadalah]." [In the manuscript it is fadlah in both places.] It was said: "The rawh is lightening of the reckoning, and the rayhan is multiplication of reward."

It was said: "The rawh is pardon without reproach, and the rayhan is provision without reckoning."

It is said: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾ is for the foremost, ﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ for the moderate, and ﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾ for the seekers.

It was said: "The rawh is for their spirits, the rayhan for their hearts, the Garden for their bodies, and the Truth for their inner secrets."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ — ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ﴾ — the nominative is in the sense of: "For you there is peace," and it is "peace for you," i.e., safety for you, O Muhammad, from them, so do not be concerned for them, for they have been saved from the punishment of God.

Al-Farra' said: "It is certain for you that they are among the companions of the right." Or it is said to the companion of the right: "It is certain for you that you are among the companions of the right." It was also said: "Then peace upon you from the companions of the right."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ — those who are the people of the left hand — ﴿فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ — ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ — and entry into the Fire. ﴿إِنَّ هذا الذي ذكروا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾ — that is, the true certainty, and He attributed it to Himself, and we have mentioned its parallels.

Qatadah said regarding this verse: "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, does not leave any person until He makes him stand upon certainty concerning this Qur'an. As for the believer, he attains certainty in this world, and that benefits him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he attains certainty on the Day of Resurrection, when it will not benefit him."

﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — so pray, with the remembrance and mention of your Lord — ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾. It was also said: "Remember the name of your Lord, the Mighty, and glorify Him."

Al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Katib narrated to us: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, from his paternal uncle, who is Iyas ibn Amir, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Place it in your ruku' (bowing)." And when ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Place it in your sujud (prostration)." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/155.] [212]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Muqri informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim al-Nabil informed us: al-Hawsi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Abu Bilal, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Musabbihat before he slept, and would say: "Indeed, in them there is a verse better than a thousand verses." [213] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/128.]

He said: By the Musabbihat he means: al-Hadid, al-Hashr, al-Saff, al-Jumu'ah, and al-Taghabun.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ — that is, that Book — ﴿إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — purified from sins — and they are the angels.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Tarkhan related to us: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abdus informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Mahfuz informed us: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us: Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Rabi', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels who are in the heavens."

Abu al-Aliyah and Ibn Zayd said: "It is not you who are the people of sins. Rather, they are those who have been purified from sins, like the angelic messengers and the human messengers. Gabriel, who brings it down, is purified, and the messengers to whom he brings it are purified."

Ibn Abbas said: "[Purified] from polytheism." Ikrimah said: "They are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel."

Qatadah said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ عند الله إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — with God, only the purified touch it. As for in this world, it is touched by the impure disbeliever and the abominable hypocrite."

Habban, from al-Kalbi: "They are the noble scribe-angels, the righteous." Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from him: "No one recites it except the monotheists."

Ikrimah said: "Ibn Abbas used to forbid that the Jews and Christians be enabled to recite the Qur'an."

Al-Farra': "They do not find its taste and benefit except those who believe in it."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: "No one knows its exegesis and interpretation except those whom God has purified from polytheism and hypocrisy."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "Only the fortunate are granted success in acting upon it."

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata': "No one understands the realities of the Qur'an except one whose inner self has been purified of impurities in the presence of the lights."

Junayd: "They are those whose inner selves have been purified from everything other than God."

Some people said: "Its meaning is: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — from minor and major ritual impurities and from filth." They returned the pronoun in His saying ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ to the Qur'an.

They said: "He meant by the Qur'an the physical copy (mushaf), calling it 'Qur'an' by close association and extension, like the sound report that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade that the Qur'an be taken to the land of the enemy." [See Muwatta' of Malik: 2/446, and Sahih Muslim: 6/30.]

They said: "The apparent wording of the verse is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَالْمُطَلَّقاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾ and similar verses." They cited this verse as proof for prohibiting the one in a state of major impurity (junub), the menstruating woman, and the one in a state of minor impurity (muhdith) from touching and carrying the mushaf. They said: "It is not permissible for anyone to carry the mushaf or touch it until he is in a state that makes prayer permissible for him." He said: "This is the position of the majority of jurists, except that Abu Hanifah does not prohibit carrying it by its cover or touching it with an intervening barrier. The preferred view is that it is prohibited, because when he carries it in its leather covering, he is carrying it through an intervening barrier, and even so it is prohibited."

Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Dawud ibn Ali held that there is no harm in carrying the mushaf and touching it in any state whatsoever, whether one is pure or impure, believer or unbeliever. However, Dawud said: "It is not permissible for a polytheist to carry the mushaf."

The evidence that it is not carried or touched except by one who is pure is what Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jarm narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to Yemen, he wrote in his letter that none should carry the mushaf or touch it except one who is pure.

And Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar narrated from his father that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not touch the Qur'an except while you are pure." [Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/615.] [206]

And because the Companions unanimously agreed upon it.

It was narrated that 'Ali was asked: "Does one in a state of minor impurity touch the mushaf?" He said: "No."

It was narrated that Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was reading from the mushaf, and he put his hand in and scratched his penis, so his father took the mushaf from his hand and said: "Stand up, perform ablution, then take it." There was no dissenter among the Companions regarding these two.

'Ata' said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — only one who is in ablution may turn the pages of the mushaf."

Those who permitted it cited the letter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Caesar, which contained: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate... ﴿قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ تَعالَوْا إِلى كَلِمَةٍ سَواءٍ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾," the verse. [Surah Al 'Imran: 64.]

The jurists permitted it when there is a necessity or an excuse compels one to it. As for children, our companions (the Shafi'is) have two opinions:

One: they are prohibited from it, like adults.

The second: they are not prohibited, for two reasons. The first: if children were prohibited from it, it would lead to their not being taught the Qur'an, not learning it, and not memorizing it, because the time for learning and memorizing it is in childhood.

The second: although a child has purity, it is not complete, because his intention is not valid. So if it is permissible for him to carry it in incomplete purity, it is permissible for him to carry it while in a state of minor impurity. And God knows best.

﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ — that is, sent down — ﴿مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾. The sent-down thing is called "a sending down" (tanzil) by the breadth of the language, just as you say "the decreed" for "a decree" and "the created" for "a creation," and "this dirham was minted by the ruler" and "weighed seven [mithqals]," and similar expressions.

﴿أَفَبِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Deniers."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Disbelievers." Its parallel is His saying ﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾. [Surah al-Qalam: 9.]

Ibn Kaysan said: "The mudhin (one who compromises) is one who does not do what is due upon him, and repels it with excuses."

The historian said: "The mudhin is the hypocrite who softens his side to conceal his disbelief. Idhan and dahana are the same, and its root is from oil (dahn)." Mujahid said: "You want to flatter them in it and incline toward them."

Some linguists said: "﴿مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ means: abandoning firmness in accepting this Qur'an and being careless about its command, and flattering the enemy and being soft toward him in place of what is required of opposing him. Its root is from softness and weakness."

Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat said:
"Firmness and strength are better than compromise... and the cowardly fear (?)"
[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/476, where it reads: "al-Ishfaq" instead of "al-Idhan."]

﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — your share and portion of the Qur'an — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.

Al-Hasan said: "In this verse: lost is the servant whose share of the Book of God is nothing but denial of it."

Others said: "This refers to seeking rain by the risings of stars (anwa')."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Ikrimah, related to us, Abu Zumayl related to us: Ibn Abbas told me, saying: "The people were given rain in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Some of the people have become thankful, and some have become disbelievers. They said: This is a mercy God has placed. And some of them said: The star-rising of such-and-such has spoken the truth.'" [207] [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/358, and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 12/153.]

He said: "Then this verse was revealed: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ up to ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾."

The explanation of this statement of Ibn Abbas regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse is what was narrated from him: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out on a journey, and they stopped, and they were struck by thirst while they had no water. They mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Do you see? If I supplicate for you and you are given water, perhaps you will say: We were watered by the rain of such-and-such star-rising." [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat: 271.] [208]

They said: "O Messenger of God, this is not the time of the star-risings."

He said: So he prayed two rak'as and supplicated to his Lord. A wind blew, then a cloud arose, and they were rained upon until the valleys flowed and they filled their water-skins. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rode and passed by a man who was scooping water with a bowl, saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of so-and-so," and he did not say: "This is from the provision of God." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ — that is, your thanks to God for His provision to you — ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ — by denying the blessing and saying: "We were watered by the star-rising of such-and-such."

This is like the saying of one who says: "I made giving to you an offense on your part toward me, and I made the thanks for my honoring you that you took me as an enemy." So the meaning of the verse is: "And you make the thanks for your provision," so the genitive (mudaf) is omitted and the genitive-attached (mudaf ilayhi) is put in its place, like His saying ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82] and similar.

The poet said:
"The people's thanks, at the time of favors, were like the sincere she-camels' drooping eyes."

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad related to us: my father related to us: Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim, from Ali, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: "And you make your thanks that you are denying." (وتجعلون شكركم أنكم تكذبون)

And al-Haytham mentioned, from Adi, that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah: "ma razaqa Fulan," meaning "ma shakara" (what so-and-so thanked). [Cf. Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/294, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/178.]

Aqil and al-Mu'afi informed me: Muhammad ibn Jarir related to me: Yunus related to me: Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, Glorified and Exalted, indeed morns His servants with a blessing or evens them with it, so a people become disbelievers in the morning, saying: 'We were rained upon by the star-rising of such-and-such.'" [209] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/164.]

Muhammad said: "I mentioned this hadith to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: 'We too have heard from Abu Hurayrah. And one who witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, informed me that he was seeking rain, and when he sought rain he turned to al-'Abbas and said: "O uncle of the Messenger of God, how much of the star-rising of the Pleiades remains?" He said: "The scholars claim that it remains visible on the horizon for seven [nights] after its setting." He said: So the seventh had not passed before they were rained upon.'" [210] [Musnad al-Humaydi: 2/432, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/271.]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us: Abd ibn Humayd related to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Talhah, from Abdullah ibn Muhayrih, who said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik summoned him and said: "If only you had learned the science of the stars, you would have increased in your knowledge."

He said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The thing I fear most for my nation is three: the injustice of rulers, denial of divine decree, and belief in the stars.'" [Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/47, no. 279, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 6/15, no. 14632, with slight variation.] [211]

Then He addressed them with an address of warning and dread, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ — why not? — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ — meaning the soul — ﴿الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ — at its departure from the body. The soul is omitted because the context indicates it.

Like the saying of the poet:
"O my mother, wealth does not avail against poverty, when the death-rattle comes upon one one day and the chest is constricted."

﴿وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — at my command and my authority.

Ibn Abbas said: "He means: those present at the dying person from among his family, looking at him, when his soul will leave."

Al-Farra' said: "This is known from the speech of the Arabs: that they address the group with the verb, as if they were his family and companions, while the intended is some of them, whether absent or present. They say: 'You killed so-and-so,' while the killer is one of them."

They also say to the people of the mosque when they harm a man by crowding: "Fear God, for you are harming the Muslims." ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ — by power and knowledge — and you have no power to repel anything from him.

Amir ibn Abd Qays said: "I never looked at anything without seeing God, Glorified is He, nearer to me than it."

Some said: "He meant: And Our messengers who take him in death."

﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾. ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾ — owned (not subject to command), and held accountable and recompensed.

If it is said: "Where is the answer to His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ﴾ and His saying ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾?"

We say: Al-Farra' said: "Both have been answered with one answer, which is His saying ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾. The Arabs sometimes repeat two particles while their meaning is one, and this is of that type. And of it is His saying ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدىً فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدايَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, where both have one answer, though they are two clauses. And of it is His saying ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ﴾." [Surah Al 'Imran: 188.]

It was also said: the verse has an inversion and a reordering, its meaning being: ﴿فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ — that is, you return the soul of this dead man to his body — ﴿إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ﴾. Then He mentioned the classes of creation at death and at resurrection, and explained their ranks, saying: ﴿فَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ — those who are foremost — ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ra', in the sense that his spirit leaves amid basil (rayhan). Al-Hasan said this.

Qatadah said: "The rawh is mercy." It was also said: the meaning is: "then life and continuance for them." It is mentioned that this was the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: Abu Ubayd informed us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Abu Hammad al-Khurasani, from Badil ibn Maysarah, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to read this word: (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

And with his chain, from Abu Ubayd: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun. And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad informed us: my father related to us: al-Husayn related to us, from Ubayd Allah al-Basri, from Harun ibn Musa al-Mu'allim: Badil ibn Maysarah informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting (فَرُوحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ) with a damma on the ra'."

The others read it with a fatha on the ra'.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "Ease (farahah)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Joy (farah)." Al-Dahhak: "Forgiveness and mercy."

﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: "A place of rest (mustarah)." Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Provision (rizq)." Muqatil said: "It is in the language of Himyar; it is said: 'I went out seeking the rayhan of God,' meaning His provision."

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym and Ibn Zayd said: "(فَرَوْحٌ) at death, (وَرَيْحانٌ) which is stored up for him in the Hereafter."

Others said: "It is the well-known basil that is smelled."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "None of the foremost departs from the world until a sprig of the basil of Paradise is brought to him, and he smells it, and then he dies."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/276.]

﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "The rawh is deliverance from the Fire, and the rayhan is entering the abode of permanence."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "The rawh is rest in the grave, and the rayhan is entering Paradise."

Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The rawh is safety, and the rayhan is honor."

Poetry: [This is how it appears in the manuscript, and it is not in fact poetry.] "The rawh is embracing virgin maidens, and the rayhan is the company of the righteous; the 'breath' (bahran) of the rawh is the unveiling of the veil, and the rayhan is contemplation and meeting."

It was also said: "The rawh is rest, and the rayhan is deliverance from calamity." It was said: "The rawh is death as a martyr, and the rayhan is the call of happiness." It was said: "The rawh is the removal of distresses, and the rayhan is the forgiveness of sins." It was said: "The rawh is steadfastness upon faith, and the rayhan is attaining security and safety."

It was said: "The rawh is abundance (fadlah), and the rayhan is [fadalah]." [In the manuscript it is fadlah in both places.] It was said: "The rawh is lightening of the reckoning, and the rayhan is multiplication of reward."

It was said: "The rawh is pardon without reproach, and the rayhan is provision without reckoning."

It is said: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾ is for the foremost, ﴿وَرَيْحانٌ﴾ for the moderate, and ﴿وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ﴾ for the seekers.

It was said: "The rawh is for their spirits, the rayhan for their hearts, the Garden for their bodies, and the Truth for their inner secrets."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ — ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ﴾ — the nominative is in the sense of: "For you there is peace," and it is "peace for you," i.e., safety for you, O Muhammad, from them, so do not be concerned for them, for they have been saved from the punishment of God.

Al-Farra' said: "It is certain for you that they are among the companions of the right." Or it is said to the companion of the right: "It is certain for you that you are among the companions of the right." It was also said: "Then peace upon you from the companions of the right."

﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ — those who are the people of the left hand — ﴿فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ — ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ — and entry into the Fire. ﴿إِنَّ هذا الذي ذكروا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾ — that is, the true certainty, and He attributed it to Himself, and we have mentioned its parallels.

Qatadah said regarding this verse: "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, does not leave any person until He makes him stand upon certainty concerning this Qur'an. As for the believer, he attains certainty in this world, and that benefits him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he attains certainty on the Day of Resurrection, when it will not benefit him."

﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — so pray, with the remembrance and mention of your Lord — ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾. It was also said: "Remember the name of your Lord, the Mighty, and glorify Him."

Al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Katib narrated to us: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, from his paternal uncle, who is Iyas ibn Amir, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Place it in your ruku' (bowing)." And when ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Place it in your sujud (prostration)." [Musnad Ahmad: 4/155.] [212]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Muqri informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim al-Nabil informed us: al-Hawsi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Abu Bilal, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Musabbihat before he slept, and would say: "Indeed, in them there is a verse better than a thousand verses." [213] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/128.]

He said: By the Musabbihat he means: al-Hadid, al-Hashr, al-Saff, al-Jumu'ah, and al-Taghabun.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 56, verses 79–96 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ — that is, that Book — ﴿إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — purified from sins — and they are the angels.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Tarkhan related to us: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abdus informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Mahfuz informed us: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us: Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Rabi', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾, that he said: "The angels who are in the heavens."

Abu al-Aliyah and Ibn Zayd said: "It is not you who are the people of sins. Rather, they are those who have been purified from sins, like the angelic messengers and the human messengers. Gabriel, who brings it down, is purified, and the messengers to whom he brings it are purified."

Ibn Abbas said: "[Purified] from polytheism." Ikrimah said: "They are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel."

Qatadah said: "﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ عند الله إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — with God, only the purified touch it. As for in this world, it is touched by the impure disbeliever and the abominable hypocrite."

Habban, from al-Kalbi: "They are the noble scribe-angels, the righteous." Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from him: "No one recites it except the monotheists."

Ikrimah said: "Ibn Abbas used to forbid that the Jews and Christians be enabled to recite the Qur'an."

Al-Farra': "They do not find its taste and benefit except those who believe in it."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: "No one knows its exegesis and interpretation except those whom God has purified from polytheism and hypocrisy."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "Only the fortunate are granted success in acting upon it."

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata': "No one understands the realities of the Qur'an except one whose inner self has been purified of impurities in the presence of the lights."

Junayd: "They are those whose inner selves have been purified from everything other than God."
